items.name: Separation rule — gap first, rule second
items.purpose: The law that governs how any two regions on this surface are told apart, written because the previous draft made a 1.72:1 decorative hairline the sole divider in six places.
items.anatomy: Three tiers, and a region must use the highest tier it qualifies for. TIER 1 — SPACE. Every division is carried first by white space on the scale: 12dp (s3) between stat-tile cells, 24dp (s6) between panel blocks, 8dp (s2) of clear space either side of a list-row boundary (row padding 10dp vertical, so 20dp of ground separates two text blocks). Space costs no contrast and cannot be lost to a dim panel, a 6-bit LCD or 40% backlight. TIER 2 — A COMPLIANT RULE, where the instrument's grid is part of the reading. A 1px edge-structure rule (#5A7088 Night, 3.00:1 on surface #1B2632; #857C6B Day, 3.86:1 on #FAF7F2, 3.41:1 on ground) centred in the gap. Used on exactly two things here: the panel's full-bleed block dividers and the tile grid's cross. TIER 3 — DECORATION. hairline-decorative (#3A4B60 Night, 1.72:1 on surface; #DED7C9 Day, 1.34:1 on #FAF7F2) is permitted only where a Tier 1 or Tier 2 separation is already doing the work: list-row boundaries that already have 20dp of clear space, chart gridlines, the rule under a collapsed steps row. Measured and stated, so nobody has to trust it.
items.states: GRID (tile cells) — gap 12 plus a centred edge-structure cross. BAND (panel blocks) — gap 24 plus a full-bleed edge-structure rule. ROWS (sources, people, suggestions, history) — 20dp of clear space plus a hairline-decorative. CHART — gridlines hairline-decorative only; the plot has no border and needs none, because the legend above and the axis row below bound it. SINGLE CHILD — no rule at all; one block in a panel is bounded by the panel.
items.behaviour: Enforced as a lint: hairline-decorative may not be the only differing property between two adjacent regions' decorations. In practice that means a widget that draws a hairline must also declare the gap it sits in, and the analyzer rule reads the gap. This is the same mechanism as the amber lint — it fails the build, not the review.
items.modes: Night and Day as stated, with the tier-2 token switching per skin. Veld: every tier-2 rule becomes 2px #1B2632 and every tier-3 hairline is DELETED rather than thickened — Veld's separation is space (40dp block gap, 64dp rows) plus 2px structure, and a third weight of line in glare is noise.
items.accessibility: A separation that exists only as a 1.34:1 line is invisible to a low-vision reader, to a dim panel and to a printed export identically; space and a 3:1 rule survive all three. Regions that are semantically distinct are also distinct Semantics containers, so a screen reader gets the division regardless of how it is painted.
items.amber: None. Amber never separates anything; separation is structure and structure is never the light.
items.screenshot: Inside the panel, four figures sit in quadrants divided by a visible pale-blue cross with real breathing room around each, and the three bands of the panel are parted by clear full-width rules you can actually see — not by the ghost lines of the previous draft.

items.name: Ask TradeIQ — screen shell (Night, Console)
items.purpose: The container the whole surface lives in: a left-aligned transcript column on the true ground, a pinned composer, and nothing else.
items.anatomy: Ground #0B1017 full bleed, no vignette gradient (the plate is for screens with a real object; an answer is language). HEADER 56dp, no AppBar chrome, no elevation, no divider. At the gutter (s5 = 20dp phone, s8 = 40dp at ≥1080): 'Ask TradeIQ' at title.l 20/600/1.25/−0.5% ink-1 #EEE9DF, left. Right: TWO 48dp ghost icon buttons, 8dp (s2) apart — SKIN (a 24px 2px-stroke half-filled circle, ink-2) and HISTORY (a 24px 2px-stroke clock-rewind, ink-2). There is no 'New' button in the header; starting over lives at the foot of the history sheet, next to the sentence that names its consequence. TRANSCRIPT: ListView.builder, padding LTRB gutter / 24 (s6) / gutter / computed. Column max-width 720dp, LEFT-aligned at the gutter at ≥1080 — never centred. Turn gap 32 (s7); block gap inside a turn 24 (s6); intra-block 12 (s3). Question bubble right-aligned inside the column; every assistant element left-aligned to the column's left edge — that asymmetry is the only right-alignment on the surface and it is load-bearing. NAV: the app's floating pill, inset 16, 20 above safe area, 64 tall, radius 14, fill well #141D27 fully opaque, 3dp flame-600 underbar under the active slot; it retracts on scroll and hides on keyboard-open (see the keyboard item). No BackdropFilter, no ShaderMask, no ImageFiltered, no BoxShadow anywhere on this screen.
items.states: First run (no messages) → the empty first-run state replaces the transcript entirely. Transcript with turns. Streaming (Send becomes Stop; follow-up chips disabled). Offline (composer band). Session ended (band above composer). Assistant not enabled for the tenant (the gate's own empty-state grammar, never an error). Gate loading → the skeleton geometry of one empty transcript, not a centred spinner. NAV RETRACTED (the manager is reading). KEYBOARD OPEN (nav absent). Wide console ≥1080 → gutter 40, column still left-aligned, sidebar rail owns navigation and the floating pill is absent.
items.behaviour: AUTO-FOLLOW, rebuilt: while a turn streams the list is pinned to the tail by a single `jumpTo(maxScrollExtent)` scheduled at most once per frame from a post-frame callback — NOT an animateTo per token. The previous draft inherited chat_screen.dart:65 (`ref.listen(... _scrollToEnd())` at 220ms), which fires on every state change and cancels its own animation ~30×/second; that is deleted. A smooth 200ms animateTo is used only on a block boundary (a new prose block, the panel, the chips) and never under MediaQuery.disableAnimations. One deliberate upward scroll releases the follow and raises a 48dp ghost 'Jump to the answer' row pinned 12dp above the composer; tapping re-arms it. Nothing on this screen blocks on the network. An artifact that throws while painting is caught and replaced by the unsupported-view note; the transcript never goes down with one card.
items.modes: Night as specified. Day: ground #EEE9DF, header ink-1 #1B2632, ghost icons ink-2 #4A4437. Veld: ground #FFFFFF, ink #0E141A, gutter 24 (s6), header 64dp, icon buttons 56dp, turn gap 40 (s8), column max-width unconstrained (single column, Field density — Veld × Console cannot be constructed).
items.accessibility: Header is Semantics(header: true). Both icon buttons carry required semanticLabels ('Change display mode', 'Conversation history') and are 48dp — the Android floor, not the 44dp iOS one; the previous draft used 44 for an Android-first product on cheap hardware and that was simply the wrong number. 56dp in Veld. Transcript is a scrollable region; each turn is a Semantics container announcing 'Question' or 'Answer' first. At 2.0× the header wraps to two lines and grows; the icon buttons stay 48dp and drop to the second line rather than shrinking. Nothing is pinned by height.
items.amber: ONE object in the default state: the nav pill's 3dp flame-600 underbar, COUNTED — not exempt as chrome. It is object 1 of the route's budget of 2 and it is absent whenever the pill is (retracted, keyboard open, modal sheet up). The second object is whatever the arbiter has lit; see the amber ledger.
items.screenshot: A near-black page. Top left, 'Ask TradeIQ' in warm off-white; top right two thin outline icons — a half-filled circle and a clock-rewind. Below, a column hanging off the left edge: a small right-aligned dark-slate block of the manager's question, then a thin vertical line of dots, then one large sentence, then a single outlined dark panel of figures with visible dividers, then small outlined pill buttons. At the bottom a sunken input trough and a plain square send button, floating above a separate dark navigation pill with a short amber bar glowing under one icon.

items.name: The bottom stack and the keyboard
items.purpose: To state, in measured dp, how much of the screen is permanently not the answer — and what moves when the keyboard opens.
items.anatomy: MEASURED, at 1.0× on a 640dp-tall viewport. Composer block = standing label 18 + 8 (s2) + trough 56 = 82. Gap to nav 12 (s3). Nav pill 64. Nav-to-safe 20 (s5). Safe area ≈34. TOTAL WITH THE PILL VISIBLE: 212dp, plus a 56dp header — 268dp, 42% of the viewport. The previous draft's '≈168dp' did not reconcile with its own numbers and is corrected here. PILL RETRACTED: 128dp. KEYBOARD OPEN: 82 + 12 + viewInsets, with no pill. Bottom padding is always read from a LayoutBuilder over the composer's real height plus the pill's live height plus MediaQuery.viewInsets — never a constant, so 2.0× text and a 40-key keyboard both clear.
items.states: PILL VISIBLE (at rest, or after any upward scroll). PILL RETRACTED — a downward scroll gesture of >24dp slides it out over 200ms on the exit curve; it returns on any upward scroll or when the list has been at rest for 400ms. While retracted the route's amber object 1 is absent, which is correct: the manager is reading, not navigating. KEYBOARD OPEN — the pill is removed outright (it is navigation, and mid-composition navigation is not wanted), and the transcript's bottom padding follows viewInsets frame by frame so the tail never hides behind the keyboard. KEYBOARD CLOSING — padding animates down over 200ms so the transcript does not snap. SHEET OPEN — the pill is hidden and inert beneath the sheet.
items.behaviour: I did NOT take the critic's suggestion to collapse the standing label into the trough while the keyboard is up. I measured it: the label moving inside the trough forces the trough from 56 to 72 to hold it, so the net win is 10dp, not 26 — and it costs the composer's most-defended property, a label that never moves. The 84dp is taken from the nav pill instead, which is chrome that has nothing to say while someone is typing.
items.modes: Day: identical numbers. Veld: composer block 24 (label 16/600) + 8 + trough 64 = 96; nav pill 72; safe area unchanged. Veld's retraction is instant, not animated.
items.accessibility: At 2.0× every one of these numbers grows from the measurement rather than from a multiplier, because the label and the trough both wrap. The 'Jump to the answer' row and the composer are always the last two focusable things in traversal order, in that order. The pill's retraction is never announced — it is not information.
items.amber: The pill's underbar is present only while the pill is, so the route's amber count is 1 or 2, never 3.
items.screenshot: Two side-by-side frames of the same answer: at rest, a chart, then the composer, then a floating nav pill with an amber bar; mid-scroll, the pill has slid away and eighty more points of chart are visible.

items.name: Question composer
items.purpose: Where the manager types the question, and the one place on this surface that commits an action.
items.anatomy: Pinned block, gutter-wide, 12dp above the nav pill. STANDING LABEL above the trough: 13/500/1.35/+0.5% ink-2, 'Ask a question' — a real label, never a floating placeholder, and it never moves. 8dp (s2). Row, bottom-aligned: [trough, flexible] 8dp [voice slot, absent today] 8dp [Send 48dp]. TROUGH: fill well #141D27, radius 10 at the BOTTOM corners and 0 at the top, 1px bottom rule edge-control #7C93AC, min-height 56, padding 14h/14v, body 14/400/1.55 ink-1, 1→5 lines then internal scroll, capped at 40% of viewport height. Hint in the empty trough: 12/400 ink-3 'Team, stock, shelf, competitors'. SEND: 48dp square, radius 10 — fill lifted #2C3B4D with a 1px flame-600 rim when ENABLED, fill well #141D27 with no rim when disabled. The 6dp amber top bleed is CUT: a gradient bleed is emitted light and is indistinguishable in kind from the focus bloom, so it was a second lit object standing permanently on the screen. Glyph: a 20px 2px-stroke arrow-up, ink-1 enabled, ink-mute #4C6079 disabled.
items.states: EMPTY → Send disabled: no rim, no amber anywhere on the route's composer (disabled must look disabled; 1.4.3 exempt). TYPED → Send enabled, rim present, and the route's lit object HANDS OFF to it (see the ledger): at the first keystroke the landed answer's focus bar drops its bloom and falls to ink-1 + marker + weight, once and permanently for that turn, so nothing can flicker. FOCUSED trough → 2dp ink-1 #EEE9DF bottom rule PLUS a 3px ink-1 outer offset ring around the trough, in all three skins. The previous draft's flame-700 focus rule is cut (focus is not the answer, and a focus indicator that is also the brand colour cannot be counted honestly) and Day's 1px→2px width change is cut with it — a focus indicator must not be a width change on a bright ground. SENDING → trough disabled (ink drops to ink-2, caret gone) and Send is REPLACED by Stop: ghost square, 1px edge-control, a 12dp filled square glyph in ink-1, semanticLabel 'Stop the answer'. PRESSED → Night: fill lifted→raised plus scale 0.98 (never colour-only). Day/Veld pressed: flame-500 #F79742 with dark ink. ERROR ON THE LAST TURN → the label line becomes 'Ask again, or rephrase' ink-2. OVER-LENGTH → a mono 12 ink-3 counter appears right-aligned under the trough at 450 chars ('512 / 1000'); hard stop at 1000 with a 2dp bad #FF7D8C rule and a 12/500 message with a filled triangle.
items.behaviour: Enter sends on hardware keyboards; on soft keyboards the action key is 'send' and newline is shift+enter. Press 120ms, state curve. Send clears the trough and appends the question bubble in the SAME frame. Stop calls cancel(); the partial answer stays with 'Stopped.' appended in meta 12 ink-3 and no error styling. Nothing spins in the composer — the working-steps rail is where waiting is shown. With no connection Send is disabled rather than queueing; a stale answer to a live question is worse than none, and the label says so.
items.modes: Day: trough fill well #E2DBCC, bottom rule edge-control #6E6657 (5.31:1 on #FAF7F2), focus 2dp ink-1 rule plus a 3px ink-1 offset ring, Send a SOLID flame-600 block with #1B2632 ink at 8.55:1 when enabled — the route's one amber — and a well #E2DBCC block with ink-mute #9B917F when disabled. Veld: trough white with a 2px #1B2632 border all round (a 1px bottom rule is invisible in glare), 64 tall, focus a 3px outer offset ring in veld-ink, label 16/600, body 17/600, Send 56dp solid flame-600 with veld-ink #0E141A at 10.34:1, pressed flame-500 at 8.34:1, disabled a white square with a 2px border and a struck-through arrow — a shape change, because a colour-only disabled state is invisible at 40% backlight in sun.
items.accessibility: Trough is a labelled TextField (the visible label is its semantic label, not a duplicate). Send/Stop carry required semanticLabels and announce their enabled state; disabled Send announces 'Send, unavailable, needs a connection' rather than being silently inert. 48dp Console/Field, 56dp Veld. At 2.0× the label wraps, the trough grows, the buttons stay square and the row wraps so Send drops beneath the trough, full width. Afrikaans 'Vra ’n vraag' and the longer hint both wrap to two lines without clipping.
items.amber: Night: Send's 1px flame-600 rim, and ONLY while Send is enabled — which is only when the manager has typed something, i.e. when sending is the expected next move. It is object 2 of the route's budget, and it can never coexist with a lit focus bar or a running step dot, because the arbiter returns one object. Day/Veld: the solid Send block, same condition. Disabled Send is never amber, so most states of this screen carry no composer amber at all.
items.screenshot: A sunken dark trough with square top corners and rounded bottom ones, a thin blue-grey line along its base, a small caption above it, and to its right a dark square button holding an upward arrow — plain and unlit while the trough is empty, edged with a hairline of amber the moment a word is typed.

items.name: Voice slot
items.purpose: A reserved position and four invariants, so a spoken question can be added later without redesigning the composer — and nothing else, because the control does not exist.
items.anatomy: A 48dp square (56 Veld) between the trough and Send, 8dp either side, WHICH IS NOT RENDERED TODAY. There is no speech package in pubspec.yaml and no microphone permission declared, so the row is composed as [trough] 8dp [Send]. The previous draft spent 350 words on a 24-bar waveform, amplitude clamps, haptics and a 60-second self-stop for a control that does not exist; that is cut. What survives is the rule.
items.states: ABSENT — today's only state, and the correct one. It is never rendered disabled: a permanently greyed control teaches people to ignore that part of the row. It appears the day a speech capability exists on the platform AND the tenant has it enabled, and not before.
items.behaviour: FOUR INVARIANTS, binding on whoever builds it. (1) It never auto-sends — transcribed words land in the trough as editable text and the manager presses Send; a misheard question sent silently is the worst failure this control can have. (2) It is never the only way to ask anything. (3) Permission-denied shows the OS prompt once and then returns to ABSENT, never a standing error. (4) It is never amber in any state, including recording — the surface's amber is spoken for, and an amber recording dot would put a third meaning on the brand colour.
items.modes: When it exists: ghost in Night and Day (1px edge-control, a 20px microphone glyph in ink-2), 56dp with a 2px #1B2632 border in Veld, no amplitude animation in Veld.
items.accessibility: When it exists: semanticLabel 'Record a spoken question', recording announced as a live region, transcribed text announced before it can be sent. Today: nothing is rendered, so nothing is announced — which is honest, where a disabled button would announce a capability the product does not have.
items.amber: None, in every mode, in every state, including recording. Stated as a rule now so it cannot be reopened later.
items.screenshot: Nothing — the composer row is a trough and a send square, with a measured 56dp of reserved width that no one can see.

items.name: Question bubble
items.purpose: What the manager asked, held so the answer beneath it can be read against the question.
items.anatomy: Right-aligned within the transcript column, max-width 78% of the column. Fill raised #22303E, radius 14, padding 12 (s3) horizontal and vertical. Text body 14/400/1.55 ink-1 #EEE9DF (11.12:1 on raised). Every digit run inside it is JetBrains Mono per the figure rule. No border, no shadow, no tail, no avatar, no timestamp by default.
items.states: Default. LONG (>6 rendered lines) → clamps at 6 with no fade (no gradients over text) and a 48dp ghost row beneath, right-aligned: 'Show the full question', expanding in place over 200ms. RE-ASKED from a chip or the history sheet → identical, no marker; the transcript should not distinguish how a question was typed. HIGHLIGHTED (arrived from the history sheet) → a 1px ink-2 #C9C1B1 outline for 600ms, then removed (state curve). SELECTED → standard handles; the bubble is inside the transcript's SelectionArea.
items.behaviour: Appears in the same frame Send is pressed — never after a round trip. Long-press copies the question text and shows a 2s toast ('Question copied'). No edit-and-resend in Phase 0: the controller replays history verbatim and an edited question would silently diverge from what the model was told; long-press offers 'Ask again' instead, which sends the same text as a new turn.
items.modes: Day: fill raised #F4F0E8, ink #1B2632. Veld: white fill, 2px #1B2632 border, radius 0, padding 16 (s4), body 17/600, still right-aligned — the asymmetry is structural, not decorative, and survives the flat treatment.
items.accessibility: Semantics container labelled 'Your question' followed by the text; announced before the answer that follows it. 'Question sent' is announced on send, so a manager who cannot see the bubble appear knows it did. At 2.0× the 78% cap holds and the bubble grows downward; it never truncates below the 6-line clamp without offering the expansion. Afrikaans wraps freely — no fixed width anywhere.
items.amber: None, in every mode.
items.screenshot: A small dark slate-blue rounded block against the right edge of the column, holding one or two lines of warm off-white text, with any numbers in it visibly monospaced.

items.name: Working-steps rail (live)
items.purpose: To make a pause legible — what is being looked up, right now, in the manager's own words — and afterwards to stand as the answer's provenance.
items.anatomy: Left-aligned at the column edge, width capped at 32em. Header row 20dp: 'Looking things up' at label 13/500 ink-2 while streaming. The rail: a 1px hairline-decorative #3A4B60 vertical rule at x = 8dp, drawn from the centre of the first dot to the centre of the last — permitted at tier 3 because the dots themselves, their labels and 4dp of row gap already carry the structure. Step rows 28dp (Console, non-interactive so no target floor applies), 64dp (Field/Veld), 4dp (s1) apart. Each row: an 8dp dot centred on x = 8; label at x = 28 in label 13/500; the measured duration right-aligned in mono.ident 13/500/+1% ink-3 ('0.6s'), tabular. Labels come from the existing tool→phrase map ('Share of shelf', 'Stock on shelf', 'Searching the web'), never a function name.
items.states: QUEUED — 8dp hollow ring, 1px edge-control; label ink-2. RUNNING — 8dp filled flame-600 dot with a radial gradient bloom (#FFF1DE@0.55 → #FFB162@0.30 → transparent, radius 10dp) on the 3200ms pulse (scale 1.00→1.12, bloom alpha 0.35→0.55); label ink-1, no duration yet. DONE — 8dp filled ink-2 #C9C1B1 dot; label ink-2; duration shown. FAILED — a 9dp filled bad #FF7D8C triangle, apex up; label 'Share of shelf — unavailable'; duration shown. The rail never turns red; one dead source is not a dead answer. UNFINISHED — a 10×2dp ink-3 bar; 'Share of shelf — did not finish'. WRITING — every step done, no token for 12s: the last dot becomes a hollow ring, THE AMBER GOES OUT, and the header reads 'Writing the answer'. STILL WORKING — no event for 12s while a step runs: a second line in meta 12 ink-3, 'This one is taking a while'; at 30s a 48dp ghost 'Stop' beneath the rail. MORE THAN 8 STEPS — first 2 and last 5 with one 28dp row between them reading '… 4 more'.
items.behaviour: A step appears the instant tool_start arrives and slides in (opacity 0.35→1, y +6→0, 280ms, enter curve, no stagger). Durations are client-measured start-to-end, network included. The pulse is one subscriber on the app's single Ticker, and the running dot sits inside its own RepaintBoundary so its bloom cannot dirty the transcript's rows. On the turn's done event the whole rail collapses. Nothing in the rail is tappable while it is live.
items.modes: Day: rule hairline #DED7C9, running dot is NOT amber (amber is spent on Send) — a filled lifted #2C3B4D dot pulsing at 3200ms plus the word 'Live' appended to its label; done ink-2 #4A4437; failed bad #8C1B2C. Veld: no rule, no pulse, no bloom. Steps become 64dp rows separated by 2px #1B2632; running = a filled 12dp veld-ink square plus the word 'Working' at 16/600; done = a 12dp veld-ink circle plus the duration at 14/600 mono; failed = a 14dp filled triangle plus the word 'Unavailable'.
items.accessibility: Semantics(liveRegion: true) announcing 'Step 3 of 4, share of shelf' on change, throttled to one announcement per 800ms. Every dot state carries a distinct silhouette (ring / disc / triangle / bar) and a word, so neither colour nor motion is ever the only signal. Durations announce as 'zero point six seconds'. At 2.0× rows grow to fit two-line labels and the duration drops to its own line.
items.amber: The running dot and its bloom, and only while a tool is genuinely executing — object 2 of the route's budget, held by the arbiter. It goes out the moment the last tool ends, which is what frees the budget for the answer's focus object. Under reduce-motion it degrades to a filled 8dp ink-2 square plus the word 'Live'.
items.screenshot: A thin vertical hairline down the left with four small dots on it: two pale filled dots with grey monospace times beside them, one glowing amber dot with a soft halo and its label in brighter text, and one hollow ring below. To the right of each, a short plain phrase like 'Stock on shelf'.

items.name: Steps summary (collapsed provenance)
items.purpose: What the rail becomes once the answer has landed: one quiet line saying what the answer was built from.
items.anatomy: A single 48dp row at the column's left edge: an 8dp filled ink-2 dot at x = 8, then 'Checked 5 sources · 2.1s' at label 13/500 ink-2 with the figures in mono, then a 16px 2px-stroke chevron-down in ink-3 at the right of a 48dp hit area. No fill, no border, no radius — it is a row, not a chip. A 1px hairline-decorative beneath it only when it is collapsed AND the answer follows immediately, sitting in 12dp of clear space.
items.states: COLLAPSED (default once done). EXPANDED — the full rail returns, chevron rotates up (200ms, state curve); the choice persists per message for the session. WITH FAILURES — 'Checked 4 sources · 1 unavailable · 2.1s' with a 9dp filled bad triangle before the text; still not a red row. ALL FAILED — 'No sources answered · 2.1s', expanded by default, because that is the explanation for a thin answer. NO TOOLS AT ALL — the row is absent; a turn that looked nothing up should not claim provenance. SINGLE SOURCE — 'Checked 1 source · 0.8s'. TIMES MISSING — the duration is dropped, never shown as 0.0s.
items.behaviour: The rail collapses 320ms after the done event, on the exit curve, so the manager sees the last tick land before it folds. Height animates; the text cross-fades. Tap anywhere in the row toggles. It never re-collapses on its own.
items.modes: Day: ink-2 #4A4437 dot and text, ink-3 #676052 chevron. Veld: 64dp row, 2px rules above and below, text 16/600 veld-ink, a 14dp filled square instead of a dot, chevron 20px.
items.accessibility: Semantics(button: true) labelled 'Checked 5 sources in 2.1 seconds, show the steps' / 'hide the steps', expanded state declared. The rail's live region is torn down when it collapses so a finished turn cannot announce again. 48dp / 64dp. At 2.0× the text wraps to two lines and the row grows; the chevron keeps its full hit area.
items.amber: None. A finished lookup is not live, and this row is the proof that the surface's amber has moved on.
items.screenshot: One thin line of grey text with a small pale dot before it and a chevron at the far right, reading 'Checked 5 sources · 2.1s' with the numbers in monospace.

items.name: Headline sentence
items.purpose: The one sentence a manager can stop at — the answer, before any figure.
items.anatomy: Left-aligned at the column edge, max-width 32em (≈448dp at body size; a readability cap, not the column cap). headline.answer: 22/600/1.35/−0.5% ink-1 #EEE9DF. Bold runs render at weight 700 and stay ink-1 — a word is never amber and never coloured. Figures inside it are JetBrains Mono per the figure rule. 24dp (s6) beneath it before the Panel; 12dp (s3) above it after the steps row. Only the first paragraph of the answer, and only when its visible length is ≤160 characters; past that it is body text and the answer has no headline, which is correct rather than a failure.
items.states: STREAMING — the sentence types in with the caret at its end; legible the frame each word lands, and only the block's position eases (opacity 0.35→1, y +8→0, 320ms). SETTLED. NO HEADLINE (a reply that opened with a full paragraph, or a plain non-markdown reply) — the block renders at body 14 and the Panel follows; no empty headline slot is reserved. TWO SENTENCES — permitted; the cap is characters. AFRIKAANS / 2.0× — wraps to as many lines as it needs; never truncated, never scaled down, never given a fixed height.
items.behaviour: It is the first thing drawn and it never moves once drawn: artifacts mount BELOW it, so a landing chart cannot push the sentence the manager is reading. Selectable. Long-press copies just the headline. It is also what the answer's focus arbitration is measured against — but see the ledger: the arbitration reads the artifacts, not the prose, and therefore the screen reader is NOT told that the lit bar is the one the sentence is about until the server can say so.
items.modes: Day: ink-1 #1B2632 (14.34:1 on surface, 12.67:1 on ground). Veld: 24/700/1.40, veld-ink #0E141A at 18.52:1, tracking +0.5%, max-width unconstrained (single column, 24dp gutters).
items.accessibility: Semantics(header: true) so a screen reader user can jump to it. Announced as the answer's first content, after 'Answer'. Bold runs are weight only — no colour to lose. At 2.0× it is 44px type and still wraps cleanly inside the 32em measure, which becomes the limiting factor before the viewport does.
items.amber: None, ever. The existing build lifts bold runs into the accent; this design removes that. Amber is emitted light, never a word.
items.screenshot: One large warm off-white sentence of two lines hanging off the left edge — 'Three Gauteng North outlets lost on-shelf availability faster than the territory did, and all three are Shoprite-group forecourts.' — with 'Three' in a heavier weight and the numeral in monospace.

items.name: The figure rule (mono spans in prose)
items.purpose: To honour the owner's decision that Onest never renders a figure, without turning prose into a ransom note.
items.anatomy: Every digit-bearing run anywhere in the app is JetBrains Mono Medium: the whole number token including its sign (U+2212, never a hyphen), its thousands and decimal separators (locale-driven — Afrikaans is '1 284 990,5'), a leading 'R ' and a trailing '%', 'pts' or 'pt'. Inside a prose role (headline.answer, body, callout body, chip label, source title) the mono run is set at 0.94em of the surrounding role with the same `height` and letterSpacing 0, which lands mono's larger x-height on the same optical size as the Onest around it. Inside a figure role (figure.l, figure.m, figure.s, meta durations, axis labels, bar values, mono.ident) mono is at the role's own size, tabular by construction. Onest carries every other glyph.
items.states: Number in prose. Number in a figure role. MACHINE IDENTIFIER (outlet code, order ref, artifact id, error code) → mono.ident 13/500/1.30/+1%, never scaled down, never wrapped mid-token. EM DASH for absent (—, mono so it sits on the figure baseline). ZERO → '0', never suppressed. NEGATIVE → true minus. A year or ordinal in prose ('2026', 'Q3') → still mono; the rule has no exceptions, because an exception list re-introduces Onest's identical I/l and unslashed zero. A word containing digits that is not a quantity ('Stage 6', 'Shoprite U-Save') → the digit run alone goes mono, the letters stay Onest.
items.behaviour: Implemented as one more span kind in the existing inline parser (`parseInline` → `inlineSpans` in answer_view.dart), so it applies identically to streaming and settled text. CRITICAL PERFORMANCE CONSTRAINT: the parse is memoised per block index — a settled block's spans are computed once and cached against the settled flag that already exists, and only the tail block is re-parsed while streaming. The previous draft's 'one linear pass over one answer and it is cheap' was linear per frame over a growing buffer, which is quadratic over a turn, and the digit-run scan this rule adds walks every character of it. A number split across two streamed tokens must not flicker between faces: the parser treats a trailing digit run at the end of the buffer as provisional and holds it in mono from the first digit. Copy/select yields plain text with no markup.
items.modes: Identical in all three skins. In Veld the mono run is at 1.00em of the role rather than 0.94em — glare eats counters and the size step matters more than the optical match.
items.accessibility: Purely visual; a screen reader reads the number the same either way. The rule is what makes 0/O, 1/l and 5/6 survivable at 13px through glare at 40% backlight. Tabular figures mean a counting-up tile never changes width and the layout never jitters.
items.amber: None.
items.screenshot: A line of text where '34%' and '19 pts' are visibly a different, squarer, evenly-spaced face than the words around them, at exactly the same visual weight and baseline.

items.name: Streaming answer body
items.purpose: The prose after the headline — paragraphs, headings, lists — arriving token by token without ever looking broken.
items.anatomy: Left-aligned, max-width 32em. body 14/400/1.55 ink-1. Gaps: 8dp (s2) between paragraphs, 16dp (s4) before a heading, 24dp (s6) before the callout. Headings: level ≤3 at title.m 16/600/1.30 ink-1; level ≥4 at label 13/500 ink-2. Bullets: a 16dp marker column holding a 4dp filled ink-3 square (not a dot, not an emoji, never an icon), 5dp between items. Numbered lists: a 24dp marker column with the number in mono.ident ink-3 and a period. Inline code: mono at 0.9em on a well #141D27 wash, 3dp horizontal padding, radius 0. Fenced code: a block at well fill, radius 10, padding 12, mono 13/400/1.45 ink-1, horizontal scroll inside its own container — the page body never scrolls sideways. STREAMING CARET: a 2dp × 16dp ink-2 bar at the end of the last written run, blinking at 1000ms, riding whichever block is last.
items.states: Streaming (caret present). Settled (caret gone, whole answer selectable). An unclosed bold/italic/fence mid-stream is hidden or provisionally styled, never raw asterisks; once the turn ends an unclosed marker prints as the character it is. A ```followups fence is hidden entirely while unclosed so backticks never flash. Empty answer with artifacts only → no empty prose block reserved. Plain reply that used no conventions → one selectable run, exactly as replies have always rendered. Very long answer (>40 blocks) → nothing truncated; the transcript grows and the tail-pin keeps it in view.
items.behaviour: Blocks mount with opacity 0.35→1 and y +8→0 over 320ms on the enter curve, 40ms stagger. A finished answer scrolled back into view does not re-animate. PERFORMANCE: the caret's block sits in its own RepaintBoundary so a 1000ms blink cannot repaint a 40-block answer; settled blocks are const-constructed from cached spans and rebuild zero times per frame; the tail block is the only one re-parsed. No blur, no shadow, no gradient inside the transcript list.
items.modes: Day: ink-1 #1B2632, code wash well #E2DBCC, markers ink-3 #676052. Veld: body 17/600/1.60, markers 3dp squares in veld-ink, code block white with a 2px #1B2632 border and radius 0, caret 3dp × 20dp solid veld-ink that does NOT blink — it is simply present until the turn ends.
items.accessibility: Headings are Semantics(header: true). Lists announce their item count. The caret is ExcludeSemantics. The whole prose group is inside one SelectionArea so a manager can copy an answer as continuous text. At 2.0× the 32em measure holds and the column grows; nothing is clamped by height.
items.amber: None. Not the caret, not a marker, not an inline emphasis. The existing build tints list bullets with the accent; this removes it.
items.screenshot: Two or three paragraphs of warm off-white text at a comfortable reading width, a short heavier sub-heading, and a short list whose markers are tiny grey squares, with a thin pale bar blinking at the end of the last word.

items.name: 'What explains it' callout
items.purpose: The one cause the answer turns on, set apart so it cannot be skimmed past — without becoming a box, a badge or a warning.
items.anatomy: No container at all. A knocked-out rule: a 1px hairline-decorative #3A4B60 running the full column width with the words 'WHAT EXPLAINS IT' sitting ON it at eyebrow 11/700/1.10/+8% uppercase ink-2, left, the rule knocked out 12dp either side of the text. Tier 3 is correct here: the 24dp of clear space above and below, and the uppercase eyebrow, are the separation; the rule is the ornament. 12dp (s3) beneath the rule, body at body 14/400/1.55 ink-1, max-width 32em. 24dp (s6) above the rule, 24dp below the body. If the model supplied its own kicker (the blockquote's bold first line) it REPLACES 'WHAT EXPLAINS IT' — still uppercase, still ink-2, truncated at 32 characters.
items.states: Default. Streaming (caret rides the body). NO CALLOUT (most answers) — the block is absent; no empty slot. SECOND AND SUBSEQUENT blockquotes in one answer → plain body paragraphs. The rule is client-enforced: one callout per answer, because a screen with three 'the one thing' regions has none. KICKER ONLY → the rule renders and the block ends. BODY ONLY → 'WHAT EXPLAINS IT' is used. VERY LONG BODY (>400 chars) → renders in full; clamping the explanation would defeat the block.
items.behaviour: Arrives as a block with the standard 320ms mount. It is deliberately the only element that interrupts the prose column's rhythm, and it does it with a rule rather than a colour — which is what keeps it from being read as a warning. Selectable. Long-press copies the kicker and body together.
items.modes: Day: rule #DED7C9, eyebrow ink-2 #4A4437, body ink-1 #1B2632. Veld: the rule becomes 2px #1B2632, the eyebrow 14/700 veld-ink-2 #4A4437, body 17/600 veld-ink, 40dp (s8) above and below.
items.accessibility: The eyebrow is Semantics(header: true), so the callout is reachable by heading navigation and announces as 'What explains it' before its body. No colour, no glyph and no fill carries meaning here — the structure does, and it survives greyscale, sun and a screen reader identically. At 2.0× the eyebrow wraps and the rule reflows beneath it rather than colliding.
items.amber: None. This is the block most likely to attract an amber left bar or kicker; it gets neither. The existing build draws it as a warn-washed box with a '!' tile — that box is removed entirely, deleting a colour that read as a severity.
items.screenshot: A thin horizontal line across the column, broken near the left where small uppercase letter-spaced grey text reads 'WHAT EXPLAINS IT', and two lines of body text beneath it — no box, no tint, no icon.

items.name: Instrument Panel
items.purpose: The single surface that holds the answer's internal figures, so the eye's path is forced: one sentence, one panel, one lit object.
items.anatomy: Night: fill surface #1B2632, radius 14, a 1px edge-structure #5A7088 outline (tuned to exactly 3.00:1 on the fill), NO shadow, NO rim — the direction spec's 1px Palladian@10% top rim is CUT here, because the spec's own device-floor argument says an 8–12% alpha step is below what a 6-bit LCD at 40% backlight resolves, and it cost a second border paint per panel to say nothing. Padding 16 (s4), set with padding-inline/padding-block so a shorthand can never zero the side gutters. Full column width. BLOCKS in a fixed order — (1) stat tiles, (2) ranked bars, (3) trend chart, (4) any other view-spec card in arrival order — separated by 24dp (s6) of clear space with a full-bleed 1px edge-structure #5A7088 rule centred in it (block margin −16 horizontal). The previous draft used a 1.72:1 hairline as the sole divider with no gap; that is corrected per the separation rule. Each block after the first carries an eyebrow 11/700/+8% ink-2 at its top-left naming it ('WORST FIRST', 'OVER TIME'). Exactly one Panel per answer.
items.states: Default. SINGLE BLOCK — no rules, no eyebrow; a panel holding one chart is still a panel. EMPTY — never rendered. LOADING — the skeleton state. PARTIAL — artifacts arrive one at a time and the panel GROWS downward; blocks never reorder once mounted, because a panel that reshuffles under a reading eye is worse than a suboptimal order. PATCHED — an artifact with an id already present replaces its block in place with a 200ms cross-fade, no re-animation of its figures, and a reconciliation line on every figure that changed. BROKEN CARD — one block replaced by the unsupported-view note. SUPPRESSED FOR UNKNOWN PROVENANCE — the whole panel is dropped; see the unprovenanced-figures rule.
items.behaviour: The panel's own arrival is a 320ms mount (opacity 0.35→1, y +8→0). Its internal blocks stagger at 40ms. Count-up runs from ONE AnimationController per visible panel, not one per tile. Nothing re-animates on scroll. ORDER CHANGE REQUIRED IN CODE: `arrangeAnswerArtifacts` currently ranks ranked_bars last and everything else middle; this design needs stat_tiles 0, ranked_bars 1, all others 2, so bars sit above the chart as the direction specifies. That changes an existing test's expectations.
items.modes: Day: fill #FAF7F2, radius 14, 1px edge-structure #857C6B (3.86:1 on the fill, 3.41:1 on ground), sh1 (0 1 2 rgba(27,38,50,.06)), block rules edge-structure #857C6B. Veld: white fill, radius 0, 2px #1B2632 border, padding 24 (s6), block separators 2px #1B2632, block gap 40 (s8), no rim, no shadow, no gradient.
items.accessibility: Semantics container labelled 'Figures for this answer'; each block announces its eyebrow as a header. One focus group for keyboard traversal on web consoles. At 2.0× the panel grows and the tile grid collapses on a LayoutBuilder width threshold, not on a text-scale guess.
items.amber: At most ONE amber object inside the panel, and only when the route's arbiter has lit it here — either the single focus bar in the ranked block OR the primary line series in the trend block, never both, and never while the composer's trough holds text. If the panel holds only stat tiles it holds no amber at all. The panel's own outline and rules are never amber.
items.screenshot: A single dark blue-grey rounded rectangle with a clearly visible lighter outline, divided by two clean full-width rules with real space around them into three bands: four figures in a 2×2 grid separated by a visible cross, a short stack of bars, and a small line chart.

items.name: Stat tile cell
items.purpose: One figure with its label, its movement and what it is measured against — as a cell in an instrument, not a card.
items.anatomy: No card, no border, no shadow, no radius. Cells are separated by 12dp (s3) of clear space with a 1px edge-structure #5A7088 rule centred in it, forming a visible cross — space carries the division, the rule carries the instrument's grammar, and the rule is compliant at 3.00:1 rather than the 1.72:1 hairline the previous draft used alone. 2×2 grid inside the panel; 5 or 6 tiles make a 2×3. GEOMETRY, checked on the target device: at 360dp the column is 320, the panel inner width is 288, and each cell is (288 − 12) / 2 = 138dp. The collapse threshold is therefore inner width < 272dp, not the previous draft's 320dp, which would have made 2×2 impossible on every phone the product ships to while the anatomy, the skeleton and the screen-reader script all described a 2×2. Contents, top to bottom: EYEBROW 11/700/1.10/+8% uppercase ink-2, up to 2 lines, wraps (never truncates — Afrikaans p90 is 1.40×). 8dp. FIGURE at figure.l 32/600/1.05/−1% JetBrains Mono tabular ink-1, with compact locale formatting chosen first ('R 1,28 mln'), then a glyph-count fitting rule (≤6 glyphs → 32; 7–9 → 26; 10+ → 22 with the unit demoted to a 13/500 ink-3 suffix), hard single line, FittedBox(scaleDown) floored at 18px. 6dp. DELTA on one baseline: an 8dp solid triangle (up/down) or an 8×2dp bar (flat) — shape carries the direction — then the value at 13/600 mono in good #6FE0AE (8.30:1 on raised) or bad #FF7D8C (5.49:1) or ink-3. Sentiment is the server's verdict, never inferred from the sign: more stock-outs going up is bad. 4dp. COMPARED-TO at meta 12/400/1.40 ink-3 ('vs last month'). Optional METER, 3dp tall, full cell width: track lifted #2C3B4D, fill chart-neutral #8B8271 (3.01:1 on track), target a 2dp ink-1 tick that BREAKS the track's top edge by 2dp so it has a silhouette.
items.states: Default. COUNTING UP — 600ms ease-out-quart on mount, formatted in its unit every frame, last frame exactly the true value. SETTLED — never re-animates. NO DELTA — the delta row is absent and the compared-to line moves up; the cell keeps its height. NO DATA — its own item. UPDATED — its own item (gap #398). NEGATIVE — true minus, triangle down, colour from the server's sentiment. ZERO — '0' rendered, never suppressed, never styled as absent. OVERLONG LABEL — wraps to 2 lines then ellipsis on the third; the figure never moves, because rows are equal-height by IntrinsicHeight. UNKNOWN PROVENANCE — the cell is not rendered at all; the panel is dropped.
items.behaviour: Not tappable in the answer — a tile is a reading, and a tap that leads nowhere is worse than no tap. Its expansion lives on the block's 'Open full view' row. A tile with no value yet is not rendered as zero; the block waits. Reduce-motion / battery / Veld: count-up becomes an instant set.
items.modes: Day: cross rule edge-structure #857C6B, ink-1 #1B2632, ink-3 #676052, good #14664A, bad #8C1B2C, meter track well #E2DBCC, fill chart-neutral #676052. Veld: the grid ALWAYS collapses to one column; cells 64dp minimum, separated by 24dp of space and a 2px #1B2632 rule; eyebrow 14/700, figure 32/700 (no fitting below 24), delta value 16/700, compared-to 14/600 veld-ink-2; meter 5dp with a 3dp veld-ink target tick breaking the top edge.
items.accessibility: Each cell is one Semantics node: 'On-shelf availability, 61 percent, down 19 points, bad, versus last month'. The delta's direction is in the shape AND the word; its verdict is in the word 'bad'/'good', never only in the hue. The meter announces 'meter, 61 of 100, target 80'. At 2.0× the grid collapses on the measured threshold and each cell grows; the figure's text scaler is uncapped here, because this surface has no hero figure.
items.amber: NONE — a deliberate override of the shared stat-tile component, which specifies a 2dp flame-600 target tick. Here the target tick is ink-1, because four repeated amber ticks would be exactly the repeated fill the law bans.
items.screenshot: A quarter of the panel, clearly bounded by a visible pale cross: tiny letter-spaced grey capitals reading 'ON-SHELF AVAILABILITY', a large monospaced '61%' in warm off-white, then a small solid downward triangle and '19 pts' in coral, then '(vs last month)' in small grey.

items.name: Stat tile — no data
items.purpose: To admit an absence instead of fabricating a zero (gap #399).
items.anatomy: Identical cell geometry, so the grid never reflows. EYEBROW unchanged at full ink-2 strength — the question the tile answers is still the question. FIGURE replaced by an em dash '—' at figure.l 32 in JetBrains Mono ink-3 #A79E8C (7.19:1 on ground, 5.07:1 on raised), on the same baseline as a real figure. In place of the delta row: ONE line at meta 12/400/1.40 ink-3 giving the reason in words — 'No visits in this window.' The reason string comes from the server; the fallback is 'No data for this period.' NO delta triangle, NO delta value, NO meter, NO count-up, NO compared-to line. The cell holds its full height.
items.states: NO OBSERVATIONS ('No visits in this window'). NO TARGET SET ('No target set for this outlet'). PARTIAL WINDOW ('Only 3 of 30 days have data') — the figure IS shown at full ink-1 with this line beneath it instead of the compared-to line; a thin figure is still a figure, and hiding it would be its own lie. SUPPRESSED FOR PRIVACY ('Too few visits to report'). NOT PERMITTED ('Outside your territories') — an absence, not an error.
items.behaviour: Never animates. Never renders a delta arrow beside an em dash — an arrow next to nothing is the specific failure this state exists to kill. If EVERY tile in a set is no-data, the tile block is dropped entirely, because a grid of four dashes is noise and the prose above already said there was no data.
items.modes: Day: em dash ink-3 #676052, reason ink-3. Veld: em dash 32/700 veld-ink-2 #4A4437 (9.66:1 — Veld has no sub-9:1 text token, so the dash is not dimmed to ink-3's role; it is separated by the word beneath it instead), reason 14/600 veld-ink-2.
items.accessibility: Announces as 'Stock-outs, no data, no visits in this window' — the words 'no data' are spoken, never inferred from a dash. The em dash is a real character in the text, not a drawn rule, so it is read. Colour is not the signal: the reason sentence is.
items.amber: None.
items.screenshot: A grid cell where, under the small grey capitals, a long monospaced dash sits where a big number would be, with one line of small grey text beneath reading 'No visits in this window.' — and no arrow, no percentage, no bar.

items.name: Stat tile — updated figure (reconciliation)
items.purpose: To account for a figure that changed while the manager was looking at it, instead of swapping it silently (gap #398, which the previous draft named as served and did not serve).
items.anatomy: Identical cell geometry. The FIGURE shows the new value at full ink-1. The compared-to line is joined — or, where there is no compared-to line, replaced — by a RECONCILIATION LINE at meta 12/400/1.40 ink-3 with its figures in mono: 'Updated from 61% at 14:22.' No colour, no glyph, no bar, no animation, and no severity of any kind — a figure being recomputed is a fact, not a fault. The line persists for the life of the turn and does not fade, dismiss or collapse. Where a provisional value was labelled as such by the server, the wording is the brief's own: 'Scored 71, you saw 84.'
items.states: PATCHED WITH A CHANGE — the line appears. PATCHED WITH NO CHANGE — no line; nothing happened worth saying. PATCHED TWICE — the line names the ORIGINAL value and the latest time ('Updated from 61% at 14:31'), not a chain; a manager needs what she saw and when it stopped being true. PROVISIONAL → FINAL — the same line with the server's own pair of words. PATCHED TO NO DATA — the no-data state plus 'Was 61% at 14:22.' PATCHED WHILE OFF SCREEN — identical; the line is there when she scrolls back, which is the whole point.
items.behaviour: The value changes in ONE frame at the midpoint of the 200ms cross-fade and never tweens between two real values; the reconciliation line cross-fades in with it. A READ LOCK holds for 1200ms after any animation in that panel ends, so a patch landing under a reading eye waits rather than moving. Copy and PDF export both carry the line — a correction that survives only on screen is a correction you are hiding.
items.modes: Day: line at meta 12 ink-3 #676052. Veld: 14/600 veld-ink-2, no cross-fade — the figure and its line simply change.
items.accessibility: The cell's Semantics label gains the clause in words and the change is announced once, politely, never as an alert: 'On-shelf availability, 84 percent, updated from 61 percent at 14:22.' At 2.0× the line wraps and the cell grows.
items.amber: None. A changed figure is not live and not a warning; if it were lit, every recomputation would read as an alarm.
items.screenshot: The same grid cell, now reading '84%', with one extra line of small grey text beneath: 'Updated from 61% at 14:22.' — the old figure in monospace, nothing highlighted.

items.name: Ranked bars block
items.purpose: A ranking, worst first, with the one bar the answer is about carrying four channels of emphasis rather than a hue.
items.anatomy: Inside the panel beneath a block rule, eyebrow 'WORST FIRST' 11/700 ink-2, 12dp beneath it. Rows min-height 48dp (Console/Field) / 64dp (Veld), growing to fit, 8dp apart. Row layout, measured at the 288dp panel inner width: LABEL column 38% capped at 112dp, body 14/400 ink-1, TWO LINES allowed with the row growing, middle-truncated only on a third line. The previous draft's single middle-truncated line failed exactly where it mattered — 'Shoprite Klipfontein Mall' and 'Shoprite Klipfontein Mall Ext 2' both render as 'Shoprite Kli…Mall', and the row is not tappable, so there was no path to the full string. A ranked row is a name and a number, and the name is the half you cannot guess. 12dp (s3). TRACK, flexible, minimum 72dp (84dp at 288 inner width): 6dp tall, radius 3, fill lifted #2C3B4D. 12dp. VALUE column 68dp, right-aligned, mono 13/500 ink-1 (focus: 700), with the SAME compact locale formatter the tiles use applied first ('R 1,28 mln'), then FittedBox floored at 11px, and when it still does not fit the value drops to its own line beneath the track — the layout the 2.0× rule already defines. Non-focus bars: chart-neutral #8B8271 (3.01:1 on track; 2.12:1 true, 2.11 grey, 2.21 deutan against amber). FOCUS BAR, when the route's arbiter has lit this block: flame-600 #FFB162 (6.37:1 on track), a 12dp amber gradient bloom beneath the bar drawn inside the same BoxDecoration (never a blur, never a BoxShadow), a 7dp filled triangle marker at the bar's origin pointing right, and its label at body.strong. Four channels: fill, bloom, marker, weight.
items.states: DEFAULT (all values ≥ 0). DIVERGING (any value < 0) — bars diverge around a 1dp edge-control centre axis (NOT amber); negative fill is bad #FF7D8C HATCHED with 45° hard-stop stripes (4dp stripe, 2dp gap), because #FF7D8C against chart-neutral is 1.55:1 in colour and 1.26:1 in protanopia; positives take good #6FE0AE solid; every value printed with its sign. ZERO — no bar drawn, '0' printed, plus a 2dp ink-3 tick at the origin so the row is not read as missing. MISSING — em dash in ink-3 and a hatched 6dp track segment at 20% width; never a zero bar. MORE THAN 6 ITEMS (schema allows 12) — 6 rows plus a 48dp ghost row 'Show all 11' expanding in place over 200ms; never a nested scroll region. EMPTY SET — the block is omitted entirely. SINGLE ITEM — rendered without the focus channels; one bar cannot be ranked. AMBER SPENT ELSEWHERE, or HANDED OFF to Send when the manager starts typing — focus fill becomes ink-1 #EEE9DF with the marker and the weight retained and the bloom dropped; the hand-off is one-way for the life of the turn, so a bar can never flicker back alight.
items.behaviour: Items keep the server's order and are never re-sorted client-side — what 'worst' means depends on the metric and the server knows. Bars grow in over 600ms with a 60ms stagger on mount, once. Not tappable inside the answer. Each row sits in a RepaintBoundary. No blur, no shadow, no gradient except the single focus bloom.
items.modes: Day/Veld: amber is NOT the focus channel — focus fill is ink-1 (#1B2632, 11.12:1 on track #E2DBCC) plus the marker plus the weight. Day track well #E2DBCC, neutral fill #676052 (4.52:1). Veld: track 8dp, neutral veld-ink-2 #4A4437, focus veld-ink #0E141A plus a 9dp triangle plus weight 700, rows 64dp, label 16/600 over two lines, value 16/700, no bloom, no radius.
items.accessibility: Each row is one Semantics node: 'Shoprite Klipfontein Mall, 34 percent, worst, position 1 of 11'. It does NOT say 'the one this answer is about' — see the screen-reader script; the focus is a client-side inference from index 0 and the spoken channel must not state as fact what the sighted channel only implies. The focus is carried by shape and weight as well as hue, so greyscale, deuteranopia, print and a sun-washed panel all keep it. Hatching, not colour, distinguishes negatives. At 2.0× the label takes 55% and the value drops beneath the track.
items.amber: AT MOST ONE — the single focus bar with its bloom and marker, and only when the arbiter lands here, which it does whenever a landed answer contains ranked bars and the trough is empty. Never a second amber bar, never an amber axis, never an amber centre line, never an amber value.
items.screenshot: Five rows: an outlet name running to two lines, a thin dark track holding a bar, and a monospaced figure. The top bar is warm amber with a soft glow bleeding downward and a small amber triangle at its left end, its name in bolder type; the four beneath it are a flat warm grey.

items.name: Trend chart block
items.purpose: Our series against its comparison over time, with the legend as a rule rather than a courtesy.
items.anatomy: Inside the panel beneath a block rule, eyebrow 'OVER TIME' 11/700 ink-2, then the LEGEND (mandatory, always, every render) as a 20dp row, then the plot at 160dp (Console) / 200dp (Veld), then a 20dp axis-label row. Gridlines: horizontal only, 3 or 4, 1dp hairline-decorative — tier 3 is correct, because the axis row and the legend bound the plot. No vertical gridlines, no plot border, no background fill. OUR SERIES: a 2dp line. When lit: flame-600 #FFB162 with a vertical area fill from flame-600@0.12 to @0.00 (capped down from 18% because that wash behind the dashed terracotta is the worst case for the tightest hue pair in the system). When not: 2dp ink-1 #EEE9DF with a 10%→0 ink-1 fill. COMPARISON: 1.5dp dashed comparison #E08E71 (7.52:1 on ground, 5.30:1 on raised), dash 4-3, NEVER an area fill — a filled comparison breaks the 1.41:1 deuteranopia pair that the stroke pattern is carrying. TARGET RULE: 1dp dashed edge-control, dash 2-3, labelled at its right end in meta 12 mono ink-3. POINTS: none except the last of each series — a 3dp filled disc in that series' colour. AXIS LABELS: mono 12/400 ink-3; x labels thinned to first, last and every nth; y at 3 values with the unit on the top one only.
items.states: TWO SERIES. ONE SERIES (most turns) — no comparison stroke and no comparison legend entry; the legend still renders with one row. COMPARISON REQUESTED BUT EMPTY — a subtitle line reads 'no data for last year' in meta 12 ink-3 and no second line or legend entry is drawn; naming a line that is not on the chart is the failure this avoids. FEWER THAN 2 READABLE POINTS — the plot is replaced, inside the same slot, by one line at meta 12 ink-3: 'Not enough data to plot — 1 period returned.' The legend is dropped with it. A ROW THAT CANNOT BE READ is skipped, never plotted as zero. ALL VALUES EQUAL — the y axis gets a ±10% band so a flat line sits in the middle rather than on the floor. MORE THAN 3 SERIES — every series goes monochrome chart-neutral at descending alpha with distinct stroke patterns (solid, 4-3, 2-2, 6-2); dull and correct, and the legend carries all of it. HANDED OFF — when the trough takes text, the lit series falls to ink-1 and drops its fill, once and permanently.
items.behaviour: The line draws left-to-right over 600ms with a horizontal clip (not a path-length shader, which would cost a saveLayer), once, on mount. Axis labels and gridlines appear at full opacity immediately — the frame is present before the data moves through it. Not tappable in the answer; no tooltips, no crosshair, no scrub. items.name: Chart legend
items.purpose: To make the dashed/solid distinction readable, because hue is doing almost nothing for a dichromat on the amber/terracotta pair.
items.anatomy: A 20dp row above every multi-series plot, left-aligned, entries 16dp (s4) apart, wrapping at narrow width. Each entry: a 16×2dp swatch drawn with the series' ACTUAL stroke — solid, dashed 4-3, dashed 2-3, dashed 6-2 — in the series' own colour, then 6dp, then the label at label 13/500 ink-2. No boxes, no dots, no colour chips: a chip would show the hue and hide the pattern, which is the channel doing the work.
items.states: One entry (single series — still rendered; the legend is a rule, not a conditional). Two entries. Three or more (monochrome, pattern-distinguished). An entry whose series has no data is NOT rendered. Target rule present → it takes an entry, drawn as its 2-3 dash in edge-control, labelled 'Target 80%'. Outside-sourced series → never appears here; outside data never shares a plot with internal data.
items.behaviour: Renders on every chart, every time, before the plot mounts. Never animates. Never collapses behind a control. Its vertical cost is permanent and accepted — Truffle-as-competitor is a convention nobody arrives knowing.
items.modes: Day: swatches in the Day series colours, label ink-2 #4A4437. Veld: swatches 20×2px at full veld-ink / veld-ink-2, labels 16/600, entries 24dp apart, always one per row (glare makes a horizontal legend a guessing game).
items.accessibility: Read before the plot's summary, NAMING THE CHANNEL AND NOT THE COLOUR: 'Legend: this year, solid line; last year, dashed line.' The previous draft said 'solid amber; dashed terracotta', which contradicted this document's own closing claim and handed a blind manager the one channel she cannot use. At 2.0× entries stack one per row.
items.amber: The amber swatch counts as part of the series it belongs to, not as a separate object — a legend key is a restatement of the lit thing, not a second lit thing. In Day, where the series is ink-1, the swatch is ink-1 too.

items.name: Unprovenanced figures — the Phase 0 rule
items.purpose: To make the 'outside data never enters the instrument panel' guarantee true TODAY, on the wire that exists, instead of shipping the confidence of the separation with none of the separation.
items.anatomy: No new pixels except one line. THE RULE: if a turn invoked any web tool AND any figure artifact in that turn lacks an `origin` field, the client renders NO figure artifacts for that turn at all. The panel is dropped. The prose stands alone, and one line sits where the panel would have been, at meta 12/400/1.40 ink-3, left-aligned at the column edge, 24dp (s6) above and below: 'Figures are not shown for answers that used the web, because this app version cannot tell which came from outside.' Dull, and correct.
items.states: SAFE (no web tool ran) — every figure is internal by construction, and the panel renders normally. This is the overwhelming majority of turns, so the rule costs almost nothing. SUPPRESSED (a web tool ran, no origin field) — today's behaviour for every web-touched turn. RESOLVED (the schema has shipped) — figures carry origin/readAt/publisher, internal ones render in the panel, outside ones are routed by the registry to the outside-data band, and this rule never fires again. MIXED, POST-SCHEMA — internal in the panel, outside in the band, never in the same container and never on the same scale. PARTIALLY TAGGED, POST-SCHEMA — a single untagged figure in a web-touched turn suppresses that turn's panel; there is no 'probably internal'.
items.behaviour: Verified against the code: `tileSchema` and `rankedBarsSchema` in backend/src/modules/assistant/figures.ts are both `.strict()` with no provenance field, so today a retailer-website shelf price and a TradeIQ stock count are the same object on the wire. The backend enforces the separation only as prose rules in the system prompt, which the brief explicitly forbids. Enforcement here is structural and client-side, because it has to work before the schema lands: it is a guard in the artifact registry, not a convention. Suppression is logged so the frequency is measurable and the schema work can be prioritised on a real number.
items.modes: Identical in all three skins; the line takes the skin's meta role (Day ink-3 #676052; Veld 14/600 veld-ink-2, 40dp above and below).
items.accessibility: The line is announced as part of the answer, after the prose: 'Figures are not shown for answers that used the web, because this app version cannot tell which came from outside.' It is not an error and is never announced as one. A blind manager gets exactly the sighted one's information — which is that there are no figures and why.
items.amber: None. A suppressed panel takes no light; the arbiter simply finds no artifact to light, and the route's amber count drops to the nav underbar alone.
items.screenshot: An answer that ends with its prose and one quiet grey sentence where a panel of figures would have been — nothing else, no box, no warning.

items.name: Outside-data band
items.purpose: To carry figures that came from outside TradeIQ without ever letting them touch an internal total — once the wire can say which is which.
items.anatomy: BELOW the panel, never inside it, separated by 24dp (s6). No panel treatment: ground fill, no radius, no outline. A 2dp left rule in comparison #E08E71 running the band's full height, then 12dp (s3), then the content column. EYEBROW: 'OUTSIDE DATA · READ 14 SEP' at 11/700/+8% ink-2, the date in mono. 8dp. PUBLISHER LINE at body 14/400 ink-2: 'Shoprite website shelf prices, read 14 September. Not TradeIQ data, and not added to any total above.' — that second clause is a permanent part of the string, not a tooltip. 12dp. FIGURE ROWS, never tiles and never a 2×2 grid, because the grid is the internal instrument's shape and borrowing it is the confusion this band exists to prevent: 48dp minimum rows with 20dp of clear space between text blocks, label at body 14 ink-1 left, value at figure.s 16/600 mono ink-1 right with a 1dp dashed comparison underline (dash 3-2) under the value's own width only, and a superscript source index in mono.ident 11 after it. Rows separated by a hairline-decorative sitting in that clear space.
items.states: PRE-SCHEMA (today) — the band CANNOT occur, and neither can the panel on a web-touched turn; see the unprovenanced-figures rule. That is the honest Phase 0 state, and it is declared rather than left to the 'no outside data' branch. DEFAULT (post-schema). NO OUTSIDE DATA — absent entirely. OUTSIDE RANKING — a wholly outside-sourced ranking renders here with OUTLINED bars (1dp comparison outline, transparent fill, no solid fill anywhere) so 'not ours' is legible at a glance; it never shares a plot or a track scale with internal bars. STALE — read date older than 7 days: the eyebrow gains '· 12 DAYS OLD' and the publisher line reads 'read 6 September, which may be out of date.' Never a warning colour; staleness is a fact, not a severity. SOURCE MISSING — a figure tagged outside with no citation is DROPPED, not rendered. EXTERNAL CONTEXT OFF for the tenant — the band cannot occur, because the tools are never declared to the model.
items.behaviour: Tapping a figure row scrolls to its source row and outlines that row in 1dp ink-2 for 600ms. Nothing here is summed, averaged or compared against an internal figure by the client. Enforcement is structural: a figure artifact whose origin is 'outside' is routed here by the registry and cannot be rendered inside the Panel at all. REQUIRED WIRE CHANGE: `origin: 'internal' | 'outside'`, `readAt: ISO date`, `publisher: string` on the figure artifact, plus an outside flag on inline figure runs.
items.modes: Day: left rule 2dp comparison #A35139 (4.58:1), dashed underline #A35139. Veld: comparison on white is too weak for Veld's 9:1 floor, so the left rule becomes 2px #1B2632 and the eyebrow becomes a solid #1B2632 block with white ink reading 'OUTSIDE', 44dp wide; the dashed underline becomes a 2px dashed veld-ink rule. Rows 64dp, values 18/700.
items.accessibility: A Semantics container announcing 'Outside data, from the Shoprite website, read 14 September, not TradeIQ data' BEFORE any figure inside it. Each value announces 'outside figure' as part of its label. Three channels carry 'outside' — the left rule, the word, and the dashed underline. At 2.0× each row becomes two lines and the band grows.
items.amber: None, in any mode, ever. Outside data is the category most likely to be mistaken for a warning if given the brand colour; it takes comparison, the system's declared 'them, unlit' channel.
items.screenshot: Below the panel, a block hanging off a thick terracotta vertical line: small grey capitals 'OUTSIDE DATA · READ 14 SEP', a sentence of grey text, then three rows each with a product name on the left and a monospaced price on the right underlined with a fine dashed terracotta line and a tiny raised number.

items.name: Outside figure mark (inline)
items.purpose: To mark an outside number where it appears inside the answer's own prose, without colouring the digits.
items.anatomy: Any mono figure run the server tagged as outside gets a 1dp dashed underline in comparison #E08E71 (dash 3-2) sitting 2dp below its baseline, plus a superscript source index in mono.ident 11/500 ink-3 immediately after it. The digits themselves stay ink-1 — an outside number is not a different kind of number, it is a number from somewhere else, and colouring it would make it read as a verdict.
items.states: PRE-SCHEMA (today) — the mark cannot be applied, because no inline run carries a flag. Prose figures on a web-touched turn are therefore unmarked, which the unprovenanced-figures rule does NOT suppress: suppressing an answer's sentences would leave the manager with nothing, where suppressing its panel leaves her the reading. This asymmetry is deliberate and it is the residual risk of Phase 0, stated rather than hidden. TAGGED OUTSIDE (post-schema). UNTAGGED — no mark. TAGGED BUT UNCITED → the client refuses to render the figure, shows an em dash in its place and, in meta 12 ink-3 beneath the paragraph, 'One figure was dropped because its source could not be cited.' MULTIPLE in one sentence → each gets its own index, shared with the Sources list. SELECTION/COPY → the copied text carries the number and the index in brackets, 'R 34,99 [3]'.
items.behaviour: Applied by the same memoised inline span pass as the figure rule, so it works identically while streaming and once settled. Tapping the figure (a 48dp hit area around the run) scrolls to and outlines its source row. Never animates.
items.modes: Day: dashed underline #A35139. Veld: a 2px dashed veld-ink underline and the index at 14/500 veld-ink-2 — the comparison hue is dropped because Veld has no token under 9:1.
items.accessibility: The run announces as 'R 34,99, outside figure, source 3'. The word 'outside' is spoken; the underline is not the only signal. The dashed underline is 1dp and decorative, never the sole identifier.
items.amber: None.
items.screenshot: A sentence of body text in which the price 'R 34,99' is monospaced, underlined with a fine broken terracotta line, and followed by a tiny raised '3'.

items.name: Cited sources list
items.purpose: Where the answer's outside facts came from, tappable, after the answer.
items.anatomy: Below the follow-up chips, 24dp (s6) above. A knocked-out rule with 'SOURCES' at eyebrow 11/700/+8% ink-2 on it, knocked out 12dp either side — the same grammar as the callout, so the surface has exactly two section markers and they look like each other. 12dp beneath the rule, then the rows, each with 10dp of vertical padding so 20dp of clear ground separates two rows' text, and a 1px hairline-decorative in that space. Column width is the transcript column, not the 32em prose measure — a URL row wants the space. No card, no border, no radius around the group.
items.states: WITH SOURCES (1–10; the wire caps at 10). MORE THAN 4 → 4 rows plus a 48dp ghost row 'Show all 9 sources', expanding in place over 200ms. ZERO on a turn that did not search — the whole group is absent, header included. ZERO on a turn that DID run webSearch — the header renders with one line at meta 12 ink-3: 'The web search returned nothing usable.' An empty 'Sources' header with nothing under it is never shown. ERRORED TURN — absent. STREAMING — absent until the sources event arrives, which is after the last token; it mounts with the standard 320ms arrival.
items.behaviour: Mounts once, does not re-animate. Scroll target for the outside-data band's and inline marks' taps; the targeted row outlines in 1dp ink-2 for 600ms.
items.modes: Day: rule #DED7C9, eyebrow ink-2 #4A4437. Veld: 2px rule, eyebrow 14/700, rows 64dp separated by 24dp of space and a 2px #1B2632 rule, 'Show all' row 64dp.
items.accessibility: The eyebrow is a header, so sources are reachable by heading navigation and announce as a group: 'Sources, 5 items'. Each row is a link. At 2.0× the header wraps and the rows grow.
items.amber: None.
items.screenshot: A thin rule broken near the left by small grey capitals 'SOURCES', and beneath it four clearly-spaced rows, each showing a small monospaced number, a bold domain, and a title line.

items.name: Source row
items.purpose: One cited page, readable as a row and honest that it leaves the app.
items.anatomy: Min-height 56dp (Console/Field) / 64dp (Veld), full column width, 10dp vertical padding, flush with the gutter. Two lines, not one — a one-line row is where long titles and Afrikaans both die. LINE 1: index in mono.ident 13/500 ink-3 in a 24dp column, then the domain at body.strong 14/600 ink-1, middle-truncated at 180dp ('businesstech…co.za'), then a 14px 2px-stroke north-east arrow in ink-3 at the row's top-right. LINE 2, indented to 24dp: the title at body 14/400 ink-2, max 2 lines, tail-ellipsis. LINE 3 (only when there is something to say): page age and 'opens in browser' at meta 12/400 ink-3, ' · ' separated. No favicon, no thumbnail, no snippet in the row — the snippet is a long-press tooltip in plain text, so it costs the transcript no height. Every string is drawn as plain text; a title off the open web is never parsed as markdown.
items.states: DEFAULT. PRESSED — the whole row fills lifted #2C3B4D for 120ms (the soft full-width surface grammar; no ripple bounded by a radius). TARGETED (arrived from a figure tap) — 1dp ink-2 outline for 600ms. UNREACHABLE (no browser, or the platform refused the launch) — the arrow becomes a broken-link glyph in ink-3 and a meta line appears: 'Could not open a browser. Long-press to copy the address.' The row stays; it is still provenance. NON-WEB SCHEME — cannot occur; javascript:, data:, file: and scheme-less strings are dropped at parse and again at tap. NO DOMAIN — the host is derived from the URL; a row can never be nameless. NO PAGE AGE — line 3 dropped. DUPLICATE DOMAIN — rendered normally; the index disambiguates.
items.behaviour: Tap opens the platform's own browser in external application mode — never an in-app web view, because a cited page is someone else's site and should look like it. Long-press copies the URL and shows a 2s toast. The scheme is checked again at the moment of the tap.
items.modes: Day: domain ink-1 #1B2632, title ink-2 #4A4437, meta and index ink-3 #676052, pressed fill well #E2DBCC. Veld: 64dp minimum, 24dp spacing and 2px rules, index 14/700, domain 18/700, title 16/600 to 2 lines, arrow 20px, pressed a 2px inverted #1B2632 block with white ink (a 120ms fill change is invisible in sun).
items.accessibility: Semantics(button: true, link: true): 'Web source 3, BusinessTech, Shoprite reports 8 percent growth, opens in browser'. excludeSemantics on the children so the row speaks once. The tooltip snippet is excluded from semantics. 56dp Console/Field, 64dp Veld. At 2.0× the row becomes four lines and grows; nothing truncates to a single line.
items.amber: None. The existing build tints the index in the accent; this drops it — a footnote number is not a light source.
items.screenshot: A row with a small monospaced '3' at the left, a bold domain beside it, a small outward arrow at the far right, and beneath them a grey page title running to the width of the column, with clear air above and below.

items.name: Follow-up chips
items.purpose: Three next questions, one tap each — and never the answer, so never amber.
items.anatomy: A Wrap beneath the answer (and beneath the incomplete notice when there is one), spacing 8dp (s2), runSpacing 8dp. Each chip: outlined, transparent fill, 1dp edge-control #7C93AC, radius 6, height 48 (Console and Field — the Android floor, corrected from 44) / 56 (Veld), padding 14dp horizontal. A leading 12px '↳' glyph in ink-3 with 6dp after it, then the question at label 13/500/+0.5% ink-2. Maximum 3 (the parser's cap). Full question text, never truncated — a truncated follow-up is unaskable.
items.states: DEFAULT. PRESSED — fill lifted #2C3B4D, edge unchanged, scale 0.98, 120ms. DISABLED (a turn is streaming, or offline) — edge and label drop to ink-mute #4C6079, no fill; not an opacity mask, which would fail the token contract. A chip wider than the column → wraps internally to 2 lines, vertical padding 12dp, height grows from 48. NONE — most turns; the block is absent. ERRORED TURN — absent.
items.behaviour: Tap sends the chip's text as a new turn, identical in every way to typing it — the transcript must not distinguish how a question was asked, and the amber hands off to Send exactly as typing would. Mounts with the answer's final 320ms arrival, after the artifacts. Never animates again. Hidden entirely while the ```followups fence is unclosed, so raw backticks never flash.
items.modes: Day: edge #6E6657 (5.31:1 on surface), label ink-2 #4A4437, glyph ink-3 #676052, pressed fill well #E2DBCC. Veld: 56dp tall, 2px #1B2632 border, radius 0, label 16/600 veld-ink, glyph 16px veld-ink-2, pressed inverted (solid #1B2632 with white ink) because a 2px border cannot show a press.
items.accessibility: Semantics(button: true, label: 'Ask: which outlets recovered after the last visit?'), excludeSemantics on the children. Disabled chips announce 'unavailable while the answer is being written'. 48dp / 56dp. At 2.0× chips go full-width, one per row, growing to two or three lines.
items.amber: None, in every mode. A follow-up is not the answer, and three amber chips would be the repeated fill the law bans outright.
items.screenshot: Two or three outlined pill-shaped buttons stacked and wrapped beneath the answer, each with a small grey corner-arrow glyph and a short question in grey type, on the bare dark ground with no fill.

items.name: 'Answer may be incomplete' notice
items.purpose: To say plainly that the answer ran out of lookups — as a component, not as a paragraph the model appears to have written.
items.anatomy: Between the panel and the follow-up chips, 24dp (s6) above and below. A 56dp-minimum block: fill well #141D27 (recessed — a caveat sits below the answer, not above it), radius 10, padding 12dp (s3) / 14dp, a 3dp left bar in comparison #E08E71 full height, a 9dp filled comparison SQUARE glyph at the top-left of the content with 10dp after it. LINE 1 at body 14/400 ink-1: 'I ran out of lookups for this question, so this answer may be incomplete.' LINE 2 at meta 12/400 ink-3: 'Ask a narrower follow-up to go further.' The comparison-plus-square combination is the system's declared 'held' grammar: the answer is held short, not wrong.
items.states: ROUNDS (the default today) — as above. TIME — 'I ran out of time on this question…'. COST — 'I reached this question's budget…'. REPEAT — 'I was going in circles, so I stopped and answered from what I had.' Identical anatomy for each. NOT PRESENT — the vast majority of turns. STREAMING — never shown mid-stream; it mounts after done, with the chips.
items.behaviour: The client detects the server's BUDGET_NOTICE constant — a string shipped on both sides — strips it from the prose and renders this block instead. Without that lift the notice arrives as a trailing paragraph in the model's own voice, below the follow-ups fence, which reads as the assistant apologising rather than the product explaining. If the constant fails to match, the notice stays in the prose and nothing breaks; the block is an upgrade on a fallback, never a dependency.
items.modes: Day: fill well #E2DBCC, left bar #A35139, ink-1 #1B2632, meta #676052. Veld: white fill, 2px #1B2632 border, radius 0, a 4px left bar in veld-ink, a 12dp filled veld-ink square, line 1 at 17/600, line 2 at 14/600 veld-ink-2, min-height 64.
items.accessibility: Semantics container announcing 'Notice: this answer may be incomplete. I ran out of lookups for this question. Ask a narrower follow-up to go further.' Announced after the answer, before the follow-ups — the order in which it is useful. The square glyph plus the sentence carry it; colour is never the signal.
items.amber: None, and deliberately not bad/crimson either. 'Incomplete' is not a severity, and giving it either the brand's amber or the system's crimson would teach a manager that a thin answer is a failure state.
