items.screenshot: A slightly sunken dark block with a terracotta bar down its left edge and a small terracotta square, holding one line of off-white text about running out of lookups and a smaller grey line suggesting a narrower follow-up.

items.name: Unsupported view note
items.purpose: To be honest when the server drew something this app build cannot render — without a blank card.
items.anatomy: Occupies the failing block's slot inside the panel, so the panel's structure is unchanged. Padding 12 (s3) vertical. A 16px 2px-stroke info glyph in ink-3, 8dp, then two lines: at body 14/400 ink-2, 'This answer includes a view your app version cannot draw yet. The summary above still applies.'; at meta 12/400 mono ink-3, the spec type verbatim, e.g. 'outlet_map'. No fill, no border, no radius — inside a panel it needs none, and giving it one would make a limitation look like a card of content.
items.states: UNKNOWN TYPE (the server shipped ahead of the app — a normal consequence of separate release trains, not an error). THREW WHILE PAINTING (caught; the transcript never goes down with one card). MALFORMED DATA (the registry's parse produced nothing drawable). All three render identically, because the manager's situation is identical; only the mono type line differs. NEVER a blank card and never an empty panel: if this is the panel's only block, the panel is dropped and the note renders on the ground at the column edge.
items.behaviour: Never animates, never retries, never offers a reload — there is nothing this build can do. It does not suppress the prose above it, which still carries the answer.
items.modes: Day: glyph and type line ink-3 #676052, body ink-2 #4A4437. Veld: 17/600 body, 14/600 type line, 20px glyph, min-height 64, 24dp of space and 2px rules above and below inside the panel.
items.accessibility: Announces as 'Note: this answer includes a view your app version cannot draw yet. The summary above still applies.' The raw type is excluded from the spoken label — it is a diagnostic for a support call, not information for a manager.
items.amber: None.
items.screenshot: Inside the panel, a small outline information glyph beside two lines of grey text explaining that a view cannot be drawn, with a small monospaced type name beneath.

items.name: Answer actions row
items.purpose: What a manager does with a finished answer: take it away.
items.anatomy: A 48dp row at the bottom of a settled, non-errored turn, LEFT-aligned at the column edge (not right — nothing on this surface is right-aligned except the question), 24dp (s6) below the sources. Three ghost 48dp square icon buttons, 8dp (s2) apart, each transparent with a 1dp edge-control and a 20px 2px-stroke glyph in ink-2: COPY (two overlapping rectangles), EXPORT (a page with a down-arrow), ASK AGAIN (a circular arrow). No labels at rest; labels appear beneath at 11/700 ink-3 only when the row has room (≥360dp), which it always does at Console.
items.states: DEFAULT (settled turn). ABSENT while streaming, on an errored turn, and on a stopped turn (which offers 'Ask again' as its own chip). EXPORTING — the export glyph is replaced by three 6dp ink-2 dots on a 600ms travel; the other two stay live. EXPORT FAILED — a meta 12 ink-3 line beneath the row: 'Could not build the PDF. Try again.' plus a ghost retry; the answer is untouched. COPIED — a 2s toast, 'Answer copied', and the copy glyph shows a tick for 1.2s. NOTHING TO EXPORT (a text-only answer with no artifacts) — the export button is absent, not disabled.
items.behaviour: Copy yields plain text: headline, prose, the callout with its kicker, every figure with its unit AND any reconciliation line, outside figures bracketed with their source index, and the source list as numbered lines — a copied answer must stand alone in an email, corrections included. Export builds the PDF on a background isolate using the existing exporter, so the transcript never drops a frame. Ask again re-sends the question that produced this turn.
items.modes: Day: edges #6E6657, glyphs ink-2 #4A4437. Veld: 56dp buttons, 2px #1B2632 borders, 24px glyphs, labels always shown at 14/700 beneath, row height 72.
items.accessibility: Every icon button carries a required non-empty semanticLabel — 'Copy this answer', 'Export this answer as a PDF', 'Ask this question again' — enforced as a required constructor argument on the icon-button component so the 26 unlabelled IconButtons found in the audit cannot recur. 48dp / 56dp. At 2.0× the row wraps to two rows of buttons rather than shrinking them.
items.amber: None. These are secondary actions; the route's commit action is Send.
items.screenshot: Three small outlined squares in a row at the left, holding a copy glyph, a page-with-arrow glyph and a circular-arrow glyph, each with a tiny grey capital label beneath.

items.name: Open full view (expand affordance)
items.purpose: The way from an inline card to the filtered, table-backed version — offered only where it can actually lead somewhere.
items.anatomy: A 48dp ghost row at the bottom of ONE block inside the panel, spanning the block's width, with 12dp of clear space and a 1px hairline-decorative above it: 'Open full view' at label 13/500 ink-2, left, and a 14px 2px-stroke chevron-right in ink-3 at the right. No button shape, no fill, no radius — it is a row inside a panel.
items.states: OFFERED — only when the artifact's id is a real UUID (persisted) AND its type is not one of the answer-only figure types (stat_tiles, ranked_bars), which arrive with turn-local ids like 'getRateOfSale-stat_tiles-1' and have no row to reach. ABSENT otherwise — a control that cannot work is worse than no control, and a 404 reached from a chat is the specific failure this guards. PRESSED — fill lifted #2C3B4D across the row for 120ms. NAVIGATING — no spinner; the route pushes immediately.
items.behaviour: Pushes /artifact/:id rather than replacing the route, because the chat is where the manager came from and where Back must return her with the transcript intact and the scroll position held.
items.modes: Day: hairline #DED7C9, label ink-2 #4A4437, pressed fill well #E2DBCC. Veld: 64dp, 2px rule above, label 16/600, chevron 20px, pressed inverts to a solid #1B2632 row with white ink.
items.accessibility: Semantics(button: true, label: 'Open the full view of On-shelf availability over time'), naming the block it belongs to rather than saying 'Open full view' three times in one panel. 48dp / 64dp.
items.amber: None.
items.screenshot: At the foot of the chart band inside the panel, a hairline and beneath it a quiet grey row reading 'Open full view' with a small chevron at its right end.

items.name: Artifact skeleton
items.purpose: To hold the panel's shape while its figures are still coming, without pretending to be live.
items.anatomy: No shimmer, and — corrected from the previous draft — NO TRAVELLING RULE either. Static blocks at well #141D27 in the EXACT geometry the content will take: a 2×2 grid of four cells at the real 138dp width, each with an 11px-tall eyebrow block at 40% of the cell and a 32px-tall figure block at 60%, divided by the real 12dp gaps and the real edge-structure cross; a bars band of five rows each with a 14px label block and a 6dp full-width track; a chart band as one 160dp block with 3 gridlines drawn at their real positions.
items.states: WAITING — static, for as long as it takes. PARTIAL — a block that has arrived is real; the blocks below it stay skeleton. RESOLVED — each block cross-fades from skeleton to content over 200ms; the figures then run their one count-up. NEVER ARRIVED (turn ended with no artifact) — the skeleton is removed with the panel, 200ms, and the prose stands alone; a skeleton is never left on screen.
items.behaviour: The direction spec sanctions an Oatmeal rule travelling the panel's top edge at 1400ms, and on a screen with no other progress indicator that is right. On THIS surface it is cut, and the reason is specific: the working-steps rail sits directly above the panel and is already saying what is happening, in the manager's own words, with measured durations. A second, wordless progress animation beneath it says less and costs a third Ticker subscriber plus a continuously repainting row. The rail is the better instrument and it is already there.
items.modes: Day: blocks at well #E2DBCC. Veld: NO skeleton at all — the word 'Loading' at body.strong 17/600 veld-ink, left-aligned in the panel's place, and nothing else. Low-contrast placeholder blocks are unreadable in sun.
items.accessibility: Semantics(label: 'Loading figures') with liveRegion false — it must not announce repeatedly. Excluded from focus traversal. With no animation at all, there is now nothing here for reduce-motion to turn off, which is the cleanest form of the guarantee.
items.amber: None. This is the single most tempting place in the surface to put an amber pulse, and the prohibition is explicit: loading is not live.
items.screenshot: Inside the panel outline, four dull sunken rectangles in a 2×2 grid with smaller bars above each and visible dividers between them, then five short bar-shaped rectangles, then one large empty block with three faint rules — completely still.

items.name: Empty first-run state
items.purpose: To teach a manager what this thing is good at, in one screen, without a blank box.
items.anatomy: Left-aligned to the gutter, never centred. Top of the content 40dp (s8) below the header. (1) A 64px 2px-stroke line drawing in edge-control #7C93AC: a shelf — three horizontal rules of decreasing width with two uprights, receding. Not a sparkle, not a robot, not a magic wand. 24dp (s6). (2) HEADLINE at display 40/600/1.00/−1.5% ink-1: 'Ask about your territory.' 12dp (s3). (3) ONE body line at body 14/400/1.55 ink-2, max 32em: 'I read your sales, stock, shelf and competitor data and explain what I find. I cannot change anything.' 32dp (s7). (4) A knocked-out rule with 'TRY ONE OF THESE' at eyebrow 11/700/+8% ink-2. 12dp. (5) FOUR ROWS, not chips — a sentence-length chip wraps badly in Afrikaans and this is a teaching state. Each 56dp minimum, full width, 10dp vertical padding with a hairline-decorative in the clear space between: the question at body 14/400 ink-1, and beneath it at meta 12/400 ink-3 what it will actually do — 'How has my team been performing this month?' / 'reads visit history and scorecards'; 'Which outlets keep running out of stock?' / 'reads stock on shelf, worst first'; 'What is our share of shelf year to date?' / 'reads shelf audits and photos'; 'Show me any visits that look suspicious.' / 'reads flagged visits and GPS'. A 14px chevron-right in ink-3 at the right of each. 24dp. (6) A closing line at meta 12/400 ink-3: 'Read-only. Nothing you ask here changes your data.'
items.states: DEFAULT. GATE LOADING — the same layout with rows 4–5 as static skeleton blocks; the headline and body are already true and are shown immediately. NOT ENABLED FOR THE TENANT — the same grammar, different words: headline 'Not switched on yet.', body naming who can act ('Ask TradeIQ is being rolled out gradually — speak to your TradeIQ contact to be included.'), no suggestion rows, no composer. OFFLINE at first run — the four rows render disabled (ink-mute) and the composer carries the offline band; the teaching text stays at full strength, because it is still true. RETURNING AFTER CLEARING — identical; there is no 'welcome back' variant.
items.behaviour: Tapping a row sends that exact question. Rows press with a full-width lifted #2C3B4D fill for 120ms. Nothing animates on mount beyond the standard block arrival. The composer is present and focusable throughout — the suggestions are an offer, never a gate.
items.modes: Day: drawing in edge-control #6E6657, headline ink-1 #1B2632, rows pressed fill well #E2DBCC. Veld: drawing 2px veld-ink, headline 40/700 veld-ink, body 17/600, rows 64dp with 24dp spacing and 2px rules, meta lines 14/600 veld-ink-2, gutter 24, block gaps 40 (s8).
items.accessibility: The headline is a header. The suggestion group announces 'Four example questions'. Each row is a button labelled 'Ask: how has my team been performing this month? This reads visit history and scorecards' — the second line is part of the label, because it is the teaching. At 2.0× the display headline wraps to three lines and the rows grow to four lines each; nothing is clipped and nothing is centred, so the left edge stays a stable reading anchor.
items.amber: Night: the nav underbar only (object 1). Send is disabled here — there is nothing typed to send — so it carries no rim, and the content amber count is ZERO in every skin. Day and Veld likewise carry no amber on this screen at all, which is correct: the whole screen is an instruction and none of it is a commit.
items.screenshot: A dark page with a small outline drawing of a receding shelf at the top left, a large warm off-white line 'Ask about your territory.', a grey sentence beneath it, a broken rule reading 'TRY ONE OF THESE', and four clearly-spaced full-width rows each holding a question with a smaller grey line under it saying what data it reads.

items.name: Error states
items.purpose: Four different failures, rendered as three different things — because only one of them is an error.
items.anatomy: NETWORK and SERVER ERROR share an ERROR BLOCK in the assistant turn's place: a 3dp left bar in bad #FF7D8C full height, 12dp, then a 9dp filled bad triangle, 10dp, then the message at body 14/400 ink-1, then 12dp, then a 48dp ghost 'Try again' (1dp edge-control, label 13/500 ink-2, no amber). When the event carried a code other than 'unknown', it prints at the block's bottom-right in mono.ident 12/500 ink-3. No fill, no radius: the left bar plus the triangle plus the words are the severity, at the 'critical' commitment level. MESSAGE HANDLING, corrected: the server's message is NOT rendered verbatim on trust. It is capped at 160 characters, has newlines collapsed to spaces, and is replaced wholesale by 'Something went wrong on our side.' when it exceeds the cap, contains markup or angle brackets, or matches a stack-trace shape — with the code row carrying the diagnostic instead. A guarantee written in a prose comment is not a guarantee, and this is the exact path by which a 500's exception text reaches a customer's screen. STOPPED BY THE USER is NOT this: the partial text stays exactly as written, the caret is removed, and one meta 12/400 ink-3 line appends 'Stopped.' with a 48dp ghost 'Ask again' chip beneath. No bar, no triangle, no red. REFUSED / OUT OF SCOPE is not this either: the model's own prose renders as a normal answer, with no severity treatment at all.
items.states: NETWORK — 'Could not reach the assistant. Check your connection.' The question bubble above stays, so nothing typed is lost. SERVER — the sanitised message plus its code. DROPPED STREAM (no done frame) — 'The assistant stopped responding. Please try again.' — and only when no text had arrived; a turn that had already written prose keeps its prose and gets the 'Stopped.' treatment, because half an answer is worth more than an error that erases it. ABORTED (the user pressed Stop) — 'Stopped.', never an error. CANCELLED BY LEAVING THE SCREEN — nothing is rendered; the turn is simply not there when they return, and the cost stops. REPEATED FAILURE (the same question fails twice) — the second block adds one meta line: 'This has failed twice. It may be the connection rather than the question.'
items.behaviour: 'Try again' re-sends the identical question as a new turn; the failed turn stays in the transcript above it, because a transcript that deletes its own failures teaches nobody anything. An errored turn is excluded from the history replayed to the model — replaying 'Could not reach the assistant' as though the model had said it teaches it that such a reply is in character. Error blocks never animate in; they appear.
items.modes: Day: bad #8C1B2C (7.52:1) for the bar and triangle, ink-1 #1B2632 for the message. Veld: a 4px left bar in bad-solid #7A0F22, a 14dp filled triangle, message at 17/600 veld-ink, 'Try again' a 56dp ghost with a 2px #1B2632 border; no wash, no tint.
items.accessibility: The error block announces severity FIRST: 'Error. Could not reach the assistant. Check your connection. Try again, button.' The triangle carries semanticLabel 'Critical'. The 'Stopped.' state announces 'Stopped. The answer is incomplete.' and is never announced as an error. At 2.0× the block grows; the retry button goes full width.
items.amber: None, in any error state, in any mode. Severity abandons the amber band entirely: there is no amber warning in TradeIQ. The route's count on an errored turn is the nav underbar alone.
items.screenshot: Where an answer would be, a block with a coral bar down its left edge, a small solid coral triangle, one line of off-white text about not reaching the assistant, a tiny monospaced code at the bottom right, and an outlined 'Try again' button beneath.

items.name: Stalled and timeout state
items.purpose: To tell the truth during a long pause instead of either lying or looking frozen.
items.anatomy: No new container — the working-steps rail carries it. At 12s with no event of any kind while a step runs: a second line indented under that step at meta 12/400 ink-3, 'This one is taking a while.' At 30s: a 48dp ghost 'Stop' 12dp beneath the rail, left-aligned. At 12s after the LAST tool ended with no token: the running dot becomes a hollow ring, THE AMBER GOES OUT, and the rail header changes to 'Writing the answer'. The client never invents a timeout of its own: the server's 120s budget withdraws the tools and the model answers from what it has, which arrives as a normal answer plus the incomplete notice.
items.states: NORMAL WAIT (<12s) — nothing extra. SLOW STEP (12–30s). VERY SLOW STEP (>30s, Stop offered). WRITING (tools done, tokens not started). SOCKET DIED — the turn resolves through the dropped-stream path into either 'Stopped.' (text had arrived) or the error block (it had not). BUDGET REACHED — a normal answer with the incomplete notice; never a timeout screen. APP BACKGROUNDED AND RETURNED — the stream is still live or it is not; either way the rail shows its true state on the first frame, with no 'reconnecting' fiction.
items.behaviour: The three thresholds are wall-clock from the last received event, measured on the client, because what a manager waited is what the surface should describe. Nothing retries automatically. Stop calls cancel() and keeps everything already written.
items.modes: Day: identical, with the running dot's pulse in lifted #2C3B4D plus the word 'Live'. Veld: no thresholds animate anything; at 12s the word 'Working' beneath the step becomes 'Still working', at 30s a 56dp 'Stop' appears. Nothing else changes.
items.accessibility: Each threshold crossing announces once through the rail's live region: 'Still working on share of shelf.' / 'Writing the answer.' Never more often than every 800ms and never repeated. Stop carries its own label. The disappearance of the amber pulse is backed by the header text change, so a reduce-motion or screen-reader user gets the same information.
items.amber: The running dot's amber, and only while a tool is genuinely executing. The explicit rule: the moment the last tool ends, the amber goes out even though the turn is not finished — because a breathing amber means something is happening right now, and a model composing a sentence is not a lookup. This is the surface's strictest amber decision and it is worth the extra state.
items.screenshot: The rail with its bottom dot now a hollow ring rather than a glowing amber disc, the header above reading 'Writing the answer', and beneath the rail a small outlined 'Stop' button.

items.name: Offline state
items.purpose: To keep the whole transcript readable while being clear that nothing new can be asked.
items.anatomy: The composer's standing label line is replaced by a band: a 9dp filled comparison #E08E71 SQUARE glyph, 8dp, then 'No connection — Ask TradeIQ needs one.' at label 13/500 ink-2. The trough keeps its fill and its text but is disabled (ink drops to ink-2, no caret). Send is disabled: fill well #141D27, glyph ink-mute #4C6079, no rim. Follow-up chips across the whole transcript go disabled. Nothing else changes: the transcript, its panels, its charts and its sources all stay at full strength and fully scrollable.
items.states: OFFLINE. OFFLINE MID-TURN — the streaming turn resolves through the dropped-stream path; the partial answer is kept. RECONNECTED — the band is removed over 200ms, the trough re-enables with its text intact (a half-typed question is never cleared by a connection blip), and the chips re-enable. FLAKY — the band appears and disappears, debounced at 2s in each direction so it cannot flicker. SOURCE ROWS while offline — still tappable; the browser will fail, and the row's unreachable state handles it honestly rather than pre-emptively disabling a link that might work over a captive portal.
items.behaviour: Nothing is queued. An unanswerable question is not held for later, because a stale answer to a live question is worse than none — and the label says so rather than leaving the manager to discover it. This is the deliberate difference from the field app, where 'held on this phone' is the normal state; an analyst's question has a shelf life and a visit's stock count does not.
items.modes: Day: square glyph #A35139, label ink-2 #4A4437, disabled Send fill well #E2DBCC with ink-mute #9B917F. Veld: a 64dp band row with a 12dp filled veld-ink square and text at 16/600; Send becomes a white 56dp square with a 2px #1B2632 border and a struck-through arrow — a shape change, because a colour-only disabled state is invisible in sun.
items.accessibility: The band is a live region announced once on transition: 'No connection. Ask TradeIQ needs one.' The disabled Send announces 'Send, unavailable, needs a connection' rather than being silently inert. The square glyph carries semanticLabel 'Held' — deliberately not a severity label.
items.amber: Zero content amber: Send is disabled and therefore unrimmed in Night, and unfilled in Day and Veld. Offline is the warm-neutral 'held' state, the same grammar the field app uses for a sync queue, because towers go down with the grid and this is a normal Tuesday.
items.screenshot: Above the input, a small terracotta square and grey text reading 'No connection — Ask TradeIQ needs one.'; the trough is dimmed and the send square is plain, with a faint grey arrow and no amber edge at all.

items.name: Session-ended state
items.purpose: A state, not an error — with the work already on screen still visible behind it (gap #380).
items.anatomy: A band pinned directly above the composer, gutter-wide, min-height 56dp: fill well #141D27, radius 10, padding 12/14, a 3dp left bar in comparison #E08E71, a 9dp filled comparison square, then at body 14/400 ink-1 'Your session ended. Sign in to ask again.' and, on the right or wrapping beneath, a 48dp ghost 'Sign in'. The composer beneath is disabled in place — not removed, because removing it makes the screen look broken rather than locked. The transcript behind stays at full strength and fully scrollable.
items.states: ENDED WHILE IDLE. ENDED MID-STREAM — the partial answer is kept exactly as written with 'Stopped.' appended; nothing is wiped. ENDED WHILE THE HISTORY SHEET IS OPEN — the sheet stays open and readable, its 'Start a new conversation' row disabled. SIGNING IN — the ghost button shows three 6dp ink-2 dots on a 600ms travel. SIGNED BACK IN — the band is removed over 200ms and the composer re-enables with any typed text intact; the transcript is unchanged, and the next turn starts a new conversation id, stated once in a meta 12 ink-3 line at the transcript's foot: 'Signed back in. Earlier answers are still shown but are no longer part of the conversation.' That sentence is the honest consequence of the server's conversation id being lost, and hiding it would let a manager ask a follow-up the model cannot resolve.
items.behaviour: Nothing is deleted on sign-out. The transcript is in memory and stays in memory. Tapping 'Sign in' pushes the auth route and returns here.
items.modes: Day: fill well #E2DBCC, left bar #A35139, ink-1 #1B2632. Veld: white with a 2px #1B2632 border, a 4px veld-ink left bar, a 12dp veld-ink square, text 17/600, 'Sign in' a 56dp solid #1B2632 block with white ink (15.33:1) — not amber, because Veld's one amber is Send and Send is disabled here.
items.accessibility: Announced once on transition: 'Your session ended. Sign in to ask again. Your answers are still on screen.' That last clause is spoken, because a screen reader user cannot see the held work behind the band. The band takes focus; the disabled composer is skipped in traversal but still announces its state if reached.
items.amber: Zero. Send is disabled and unrimmed. A session ending is neither live, nor a severity, nor the expected next move in the brand's voice — it is held, and it takes the held grammar.
items.screenshot: A sunken band just above the dimmed input, with a terracotta bar and square, reading 'Your session ended. Sign in to ask again.' and an outlined 'Sign in' button — with the previous answer's panel and chart still fully visible above it.

items.name: Conversation history sheet
items.purpose: To get back to a question asked ten minutes ago, to be honest that this is a session rather than an archive, and — since the header no longer carries a New button — to be where starting over begins.
items.anatomy: A bottom sheet: radius 14 top corners, fill surface #1B2632, 1dp edge-structure #5A7088, a 40×4dp ink-2@40% grabber centred 8dp from the top (the one centred element here, because a grabber is a thumb target), scrim ground@88%, NO blur. Max height 72% of the viewport. Padding: gutter 20 horizontal, 16 top under the grabber, safe-area bottom. TITLE 'This conversation' at title.l 20/600 ink-1. 4dp. SUBTITLE at meta 12/400 ink-3: 'Held on this device until you leave the screen. 6 questions.' — the figure in mono. 20dp (s5). ROWS, one per question, 48dp minimum with 10dp vertical padding and a hairline-decorative in the clear space: the time at mono.ident 13/500 ink-3 in a 48dp column ('14:07'), then the question at body 14/400 ink-1, max 2 lines, tail-ellipsis. A row whose turn errored carries a 9dp bad triangle after the time. FOOT: 12dp above the safe area, a 48dp ghost row spanning the sheet, 'Start a new conversation', label 13/500 ink-2 with a 16px 2px-stroke plus glyph.
items.states: WITH TURNS. EMPTY — 'Nothing yet.' at body 14 ink-2 and one line at meta 12 ink-3, 'Your questions will be listed here while you are on this screen.' The 'Start a new conversation' row is absent. MANY TURNS (>20) — scrolls inside the sheet; the subtitle gains '· only the last 20 are sent with a new question', which is the real history limit and the reason a very old follow-up may not land. A TURN STILL STREAMING — its row shows a pulsing 8dp amber dot in place of the time (Night) and the word 'now'. DRAGGING — standard drag-to-dismiss. SESSION ENDED — rows readable, foot row disabled.
items.behaviour: Tapping a row closes the sheet (320ms, exit curve) and scrolls the transcript to that turn, whose question bubble then carries a 1dp ink-2 outline for 600ms. There is no delete, no rename, no pin: none exist server-side, and offering them would promise persistence the product does not have. The foot row opens the start-over decision sheet when the transcript is non-empty. THE NAV PILL IS HIDDEN AND INERT while this sheet is open, so its amber cannot show through.
items.modes: Day: fill #FAF7F2, 1dp #857C6B, sh2 (0 4 12 rgba(27,38,50,.08)), scrim ground@88%, grabber ink-2@40%. Veld: NO sheet and NO scrim — a full-screen white route with a 2px #1B2632 top border and no grabber (a 4dp grabber is not a Veld target), a 56dp 'Close' ghost row at the top right, rows 64dp with 24dp spacing and 2px rules, title 24/700, subtitle 14/600. A translucent veil is banned by Veld's own rules and white-at-72%-over-white is nothing.
items.accessibility: A modal route with focus trapped and a labelled dismiss. Title is a header. Each row is a button: 'Asked at 14:07: which outlets keep running out of stock? Go to this answer.' The subtitle's honesty clause is spoken as part of the sheet's own label. 48dp / 64dp. At 2.0× rows grow to four lines and the sheet scrolls.
items.amber: EXACTLY ONE, and only in the streaming-turn row's pulsing dot — the same single live indicator, relocated into the foreground, not a second one. The scrim is 88%, which composites #FFB162 to #282320 at 1.23:1 against the ground — below the 1.25–1.39:1 floor the direction spec itself cites as the limit of a 6-bit LCD at 40% backlight. The previous draft asserted invisibility at 72%; that composites to #4F3D2C at 1.85:1, which is plainly visible, so the scrim is corrected rather than the claim repeated. In Day and Veld the dot is a pulsing lifted #2C3B4D disc plus the word 'now'.
items.screenshot: A dark panel risen from the bottom over a transcript dimmed almost to black, with a small pale grabber, a title 'This conversation', a grey line saying it is held on this device, then six rows each with a monospaced time and a question, and a quiet 'Start a new conversation' row at the foot.

items.name: Start-over decision sheet
items.purpose: Carry on or start over, asked once, with the consequence named (gap #375).
items.anatomy: A bottom sheet, same material as the history sheet: radius 14 top, surface #1B2632, 1dp edge-structure, grabber, scrim ground@88%, no blur, padding 20/20/20/safe. TITLE at title.l 20/600 ink-1: 'Start a new conversation?' 8dp. BODY at body 14/400/1.55 ink-2, max 32em: 'This one is not saved. The 6 questions and their answers go.' — figure in mono, pluralised correctly. 24dp (s6). PRIMARY, full width, 56dp, radius 10: 'Carry on' — Night: fill lifted #2C3B4D, 1dp flame-600 rim, label 13/500 ink-1 (no gradient bleed; a bleed is a second emitted object). 12dp (s3). SECONDARY, full width, 56dp, ghost: 'Start over', 1dp edge-control, label 13/500 ink-2. Carry on is the primary because carrying on is the expected next move; the destructive option is never the lit one.
items.states: IDLE TRANSCRIPT (as above). MID-TURN — title 'A question is still being answered.', body 'Starting over will stop it.', primary 'Keep waiting', secondary 'Stop and start over'. EMPTY TRANSCRIPT — the sheet never opens; the history sheet's foot row is simply absent, because a confirmation over nothing teaches people to dismiss confirmations. DISMISSED (drag, scrim tap, back) — equivalent to Carry on; the destructive path is never the default outcome of an accidental gesture.
items.behaviour: Reached from the foot of the history sheet, not from a header button. The previous draft put New in the top-right corner 8dp from History — two 48dp targets at the worst-reachable point on a 6.5in phone, one of them destructive-adjacent. The critic proposed moving New to the nav pill's action circle; I have not done that, because the owner has already assigned the manager circle to 'raise a task / assign a visit' and a route-local override would make the same control mean two things. Instead New is deleted from the header entirely: starting over now lives one tap deeper, inside the sheet that already carries the sentence naming its consequence, and the mis-tap risk is gone rather than relocated. Start over calls clear(), which also drops the conversation id — keeping it would carry the old conversation's artifacts into a thread the manager believes is empty. The transcript is replaced by the empty first-run state in the same frame. No undo is offered, because none exists; the body sentence is the warning and it is specific about what goes.
items.modes: Day: primary is a SOLID flame-600 block with #1B2632 ink at 8.55:1; secondary ghost with a #6E6657 edge. Veld: NOT a sheet — a full-screen white route with a 2px #1B2632 border, radius 0 and no scrim, matching the history route; primary a 64dp solid flame-600 block with veld-ink at 10.34:1, pressed flame-500 at 8.34:1; secondary a 64dp white block with a 2px #1B2632 border; body 17/600; block gap 24 (s6).
items.accessibility: Modal, focus trapped, the title as the sheet's accessible name and the body as its description, so the consequence is announced before either button is reachable. Buttons announce primary-then-secondary. 56dp / 64dp. At 2.0× the body wraps freely and the buttons grow in height; they never sit side by side at any width — a destructive choice and a safe one adjacent to a moving thumb is a design that gets people wrong.
items.amber: EXACTLY ONE on screen, counted honestly and not by exemption: the primary's flame-600 rim (Night) or solid block (Day/Veld). The nav pill is hidden and inert beneath the sheet so its underbar contributes nothing, and the transcript's own amber, if any, is scrimmed to 1.23:1 — measured, not asserted. Total: 1.
items.screenshot: A dark sheet over a transcript dimmed almost to black: 'Start a new conversation?' in bold, a grey sentence saying six questions and their answers will go, then a wide dark button with a hairline amber edge reading 'Carry on', and a plain outlined 'Start over' button beneath it.

items.name: Person row in an answer
items.purpose: To name a person when the answer is about one, instead of printing a database id (gap #400).
items.anatomy: 56dp minimum, full column width, inside the panel beneath its own eyebrow (e.g. 'AGENTS'), rows with 10dp vertical padding and a hairline-decorative in the clear space between. A 36dp initials disc: fill raised #22303E, 1dp edge-structure #5A7088, initials at label 13/700 ink-2, centred — never a photograph, on POPIA grounds. 12dp (s3). Then a two-line stack: the name at body.strong 14/600 ink-1, and beneath it the role and outlet at meta 12/400 ink-3, ' · ' separated ('Field agent · Kasi Corner Spaza'). Right: the person's headline figure at figure.s 16/600 mono ink-1 with its unit, and beneath it a delta on the same grammar as a stat tile (8dp triangle plus a 13/600 mono value in good/bad). A 14px chevron-right in ink-3 only when the row opens a scorecard.
items.states: NAMED. UNNAMED (the record has an id and no name) — 'Unnamed agent' at body.strong ink-2 with the raw id beneath it in mono.ident 13/500 ink-3; this is the one place on the surface where an id is the right thing to show, because it is what a support call needs and mono is what makes it transcribable. NO ROLE — the meta line carries the outlet alone. NO OUTLET — the role alone. NO FIGURE — the right column is empty and the row keeps its height. SUPPRESSED (too few visits to report on an individual) — the name renders, the figure is an em dash in ink-3, and the meta line reads 'too few visits to report'. NOT IN YOUR TERRITORIES — the row is not rendered at all; the count above says 'and 3 others outside your territories'. UPDATED — the reconciliation line applies here too, in the meta slot. PRESSED — full-width lifted #2C3B4D fill for 120ms.
items.behaviour: Tap opens the agent scorecard route when one exists; otherwise the row is not tappable and shows no chevron — the chevron is the promise and it is never made falsely. Initials are derived from the name the server sent, never from an email or an id.
items.modes: Day: disc fill raised #F4F0E8 with a #857C6B edge, initials ink-2 #4A4437. Veld: 64dp rows, a 44dp square initials tile (radius 0, 2px #1B2632 border) rather than a disc, name 18/700, meta 14/600 veld-ink-2, figure 18/700, 24dp spacing and 2px rules.
items.accessibility: One Semantics node per row: 'Thandi Mokoena, field agent at Kasi Corner Spaza, 78 out of 100, down 6 points, bad. Opens her scorecard.' Initials are ExcludeSemantics — they duplicate the name. The unnamed variant announces 'Unnamed agent, reference 4f2a…' with the id spelled character by character. 56dp / 64dp.
items.amber: None. A person is never the lit object: the surface's amber belongs to a measured bar or a series, and lighting a named individual on a manager's screen is a product decision nobody asked for.
items.screenshot: A row with a small dark circle holding the initials 'TM', a name in semibold beside it, a smaller grey line reading 'Field agent · Kasi Corner Spaza', and at the right a monospaced '78' with a small coral downward triangle and '6 pts' beneath it.

items.name: Veld mode of Ask TradeIQ
items.purpose: To make an analysis surface survive direct sun, while being honest that nobody analyses anything outdoors.
items.anatomy: Ground #FFFFFF. Ink veld-ink #0E141A (18.52:1); secondary veld-ink-2 #4A4437 (9.66:1); no token under 9:1 for text, none under 15:1 for a border. Every tier-2 rule becomes 2px solid #1B2632 and every tier-3 hairline is DELETED rather than thickened — separation is space plus structure, and a third line weight in glare is noise. Every shadow, gradient, rim, blur, glow, wash and SCRIM is REMOVED, not softened. Panel: white, radius 0, 2px #1B2632 border, padding 24 (s6). Type steps by declared values: body 15→17, label 13→16, meta 12→14, title.m 16→18, figure.m 22→24, with a 600 weight floor, line-height +0.05 and tracking +0.5%. Gutter 24 (s6); rows 64; tap targets 56 minimum; block gap 40 (s8). The 2×2 tile grid ALWAYS collapses to one column. Charts: trend series 2px solid veld-ink, comparison 2px dashed 6-4 veld-ink-2, no area fill, 2 gridlines; ranked bars track 8dp veld-ink-2 with a veld-ink focus fill plus a 9dp triangle plus weight.
items.states: Every state in this document has a Veld rendering, declared in its own item. Veld-specific: no skeleton (the word 'Loading'); no count-up (instant set); no arrival stagger; no caret blink; no pulse (running step = a filled 12dp square plus the word 'Working'); no toast (a 64dp inline row instead, dismissed by tap); no tooltip (the source snippet is simply unavailable, which is correct — nobody hovers in the sun); NO SHEETS AND NO SCRIMS — the history sheet and the decision sheet both become full-screen white routes with a 2px border and a 56dp Close row.
items.behaviour: VELD IS MANUAL-ONLY ON THIS ROUTE, and that is a change from the previous draft. Solar-elevation entry is disabled here: an analysis surface is not an outdoor surface, and a manager reading a ranked answer at a north-facing window at 11:40 should not have her layout reflow to one column, her type jump two steps and her place in the answer move two screens down because the sun came out. She reaches Veld — and leaves it — through a 56dp SKIN CYCLE control in the header's icon row, which is the exit the previous draft did not have anywhere on this route: it specified exit 'on the skin cycle' while putting no skin cycle on the screen, and 'on a check-in at a new outlet', which a manager never does. Elsewhere in the app the automatic rules stand unchanged. Veld is single-density by construction: Veld × Field, because outdoors the surface's job is to let someone READ an answer they already have.
items.modes: This item is the Veld mode.
items.accessibility: Veld is itself an accessibility mode and does not replace the others: 2.0× text, screen-reader labels and reduce-motion all still apply on top of it. Targets go to 56dp; two-line labels are the norm; every disabled state changes SHAPE as well as colour, because a colour-only disabled state is invisible at 40% backlight in highveld sun. The skin control announces its current and next state: 'Display mode, Veld. Switch to Night.'
items.amber: EXACTLY ONE per screen at most, always the same object: the composer's Send block, solid flame-600 carrying veld-ink at 10.34:1, pressed flame-500 at 8.34:1 — and only while Send is enabled, so a screen with an empty trough carries none. Burning Flame on white is 1.79:1, so in Veld it cannot be a line, an icon, a border or a word anywhere — not the focus bar, not the trend series, not the running step, not a chip. Every focus channel falls back to veld-ink fill plus a marker plus weight.
items.screenshot: The same answer on stark white: heavy black type, a hard-edged black-bordered panel with thick black rules and wide air between its bands, one solid black bar among grey ones, a black solid line and a black dashed line on the chart with a thick legend — and a single amber block at the bottom with black type on it, lit only because something has been typed.

items.name: The amber ledger
items.purpose: The counted budget for this surface, state by state, with nothing exempt and nothing asserted away — because the previous ledger declared a maximum of one and then excused the two objects that were on screen permanently.
items.anatomy: NIGHT: A MAXIMUM OF TWO AMBER OBJECTS, COUNTED, WITH NO CHROME EXEMPTION. SLOT 1 — WAYFINDING: the nav pill's 3dp flame-600 active underbar. It is counted. It is present only while the pill is (absent when the pill is retracted by scroll, when the keyboard is open, and when a modal route is up), so its cost is real and it is often zero. It is NOT suppressed on this route: the underbar is the app's global wayfinding and making it mean something different on one screen is a worse lie than spending an object on it. SLOT 2 — THE ONE THING: a single arbiter, `litObject(routeState)`, returns exactly one of — the running step dot and its bloom (a tool is executing); the focus bar or the trend series (a landed answer, trough empty, no hand-off yet); Send's 1px rim (Send is enabled, i.e. the manager has typed something); or nothing. It cannot return two, so the count cannot exceed two, and there is nothing to excuse. THREE THINGS WERE CUT to make this true: Send's 6dp amber top bleed (an emitted gradient is indistinguishable in kind from the focus bloom, so it was a permanent third object); the focused trough's 2dp flame-700 rule (focus is now 2dp ink-1 plus a 3px ink-1 offset ring, in every skin — which also fixes Day's width-change-only focus indicator); and the decision sheet's primary bleed. DAY AND VELD: at most ONE, always Send's block, and only while it is enabled — so a landed answer with an empty trough carries no amber at all, which is correct, because a light ground does not need a torch.
items.states: EMPTY FIRST RUN — 1 (nav only; Send disabled). THINKING — 2 (nav + the dot). WRITING — 1 (nav). LANDED WITH BARS, TROUGH EMPTY — 2 (nav + the focus bar). LANDED, TROUGH EMPTY, PILL RETRACTED BY SCROLL — 1. LANDED WITH A CHART ONLY — 2. LANDED WITH TILES ONLY — 1 (nav; nothing is lit, because four numbers together are the reading and lighting one would misdirect). TYPING A FOLLOW-UP — 1 (Send's rim; the pill is gone with the keyboard and the focus bar has handed off). ERROR — 1. OFFLINE — 1. SESSION ENDED — 1. PANEL SUPPRESSED FOR UNKNOWN PROVENANCE — 1. HISTORY SHEET OPEN — 1 (the streaming dot inside the sheet; the pill is hidden). DECISION SHEET OPEN — 1 (the primary's rim; the pill is hidden). SCRIMMED TRANSCRIPT BEHIND A SHEET — the scrim is 88%, which composites flame-600 to #282320 at 1.23:1 against the ground, below the 6-bit device floor the direction spec itself cites. That is a measurement, replacing the previous draft's false claim that a 72% scrim (1.85:1, a plainly visible warm brown) made amber invisible.
items.behaviour: THE HAND-OFF: when the trough goes from empty to non-empty, the landed answer's focus object drops its bloom and falls to ink-1 plus its marker plus its weight — once, permanently for that turn, so it can never flicker back alight. The attention has moved from reading to asking, and the light moves with it. THREE OVERRIDES against shared components, each recorded here: the stat tile's target tick is ink-1 rather than flame-600 (four repeated ticks would be the banned repeated fill); the ranked-bar diverging centre axis is edge-control; the follow-up chips and source indices carry no amber. ENFORCEMENT is the per-skin lint plus one runtime assertion: `assert(collectLitObjects(context).length <= 2)` in Night and `<= 1` in Day/Veld, evaluated in debug on every frame of a golden test. Violations fail the build, not the review.
items.modes: Stated above for all three.
items.accessibility: Every amber object also carries a non-colour channel: the running dot has a silhouette and a spoken 'Live'; the focus bar has a triangle marker, a weight shift and its rank spoken; the trend series has a stroke pattern and a legend entry naming the pattern, not the hue; Send's rim is backed by its enabled state being announced. Amber is never the only signal for anything, which is what lets the budget be this small without losing information.
items.amber: This item is the count.
items.screenshot: Not a screen — a rule. On a landed answer with the pill visible, exactly two warm marks exist: a short bar under one nav icon, and either one bar in the ranked list or one line on the chart. Start typing and the second one goes out and reappears as a hairline around the send square.

items.name: Motion and the frozen-figure rule
items.purpose: To let the surface feel alive while it works and go completely still once it lands — and to guarantee a figure never moves while it is being read.
items.anatomy: Durations from the scale ONLY: 120 (press), 200 (element enter, chip select, cross-fade, block-boundary scroll, keyboard padding), 320 (block arrival, sheet, collapse), 600 (count-up, bar grow, chart draw, busy dots), 3200 (the live pulse). The previous draft's 220ms auto-follow was off the scale and is now 200. The 1400ms skeleton rule is deleted from this surface with the travelling rule itself. Curves: enter cubic-bezier(0.05,0.70,0.10,1.00); exit cubic-bezier(0.30,0.00,0.80,0.15); state cubic-bezier(0.20,0.00,0.00,1.00); count-up ease-out-quart. Stagger 40ms for prose blocks, 60ms for bars, 80ms for tiles.
items.states: LIVE (a turn is streaming) — arrivals, the pulse, the caret. SETTLING (the panel mounts) — count-up, bar grow, chart draw, once. SETTLED — nothing moves. RE-ENTERED (a finished answer scrolled back into view) — nothing animates. PATCHED — a 200ms cross-fade with the number changing in ONE frame at the midpoint, plus its reconciliation line; no re-run of the count-up. READ LOCK — for 1200ms after the last animation on a panel ends, no artifact patch may animate anything in it. REDUCE-MOTION / BATTERY SAVER / VELD — every one of the above becomes an instant set, the tail-pin uses jumpTo unconditionally, and the pulse degrades to a filled square plus the word 'Working'.
items.behaviour: THE FROZEN-FIGURE RULE, in three parts. (1) A figure animates exactly once, on first mount, and only while on screen. (2) A figure never tweens between two REAL values: 71 to 84 would display dozens of numbers that were never true, so a changed value swaps in one frame — and says so in its reconciliation line. (3) Nothing animates while a selection is active. Implementation: a per-artifact settled flag keyed by artifact id in an InheritedWidget above the transcript; artifacts currently re-animate on rebuild, which this fixes. PERFORMANCE BUDGET, with the three costs the previous draft asserted away now paid: (a) THE TAIL-PIN is a single jumpTo scheduled at most once per frame, replacing chat_screen.dart's `ref.listen(... _scrollToEnd())` animateTo, which fired ~30×/second each call cancelling the last; a 200ms animateTo is used only on a block boundary and never under disableAnimations. (b) INLINE PARSING is memoised per block index against the settled flag; only the tail block is re-parsed, so a growing buffer is not re-walked every frame — including by the figure rule's digit scan. (c) REPAINT BOUNDARIES on the caret's block, the rail's running dot, every ranked-bar row, and each panel block. Plus: one Ticker with two subscribers (3200 pulse, 600 busy dots); one AnimationController per visible panel; zero BackdropFilter, ShaderMask, ImageFiltered and saveLayer; zero BoxShadow in Night; no blur, shadow or gradient inside the transcript ListView's rows; at most 3 gradient decorations on a landed answer (one focus bloom OR one area fill, the rail dot bloom, and nothing else — Send's bleed is cut). Target ≤8ms build+paint inside the 16.6ms frame on a Snapdragon 4xx at 1080×2340, with a profile test failing the build if frameRasterizerTime p95 exceeds 12ms.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: identical durations; the pulse is a lifted #2C3B4D disc. Veld: all motion off, count-up instant, caret static, no cross-fades — a patched artifact simply changes, and its reconciliation line simply appears.
items.accessibility: MediaQuery.disableAnimations governs every one of these, including the scroll behaviour, not a custom setting. Every motion-coded meaning has a text equivalent: the pulse degrades to 'Live'/'Working'; the caret's absence is backed by the collapsed steps row; the count-up carries no information the settled figure does not. No motion on this surface is ever the only signal for anything.
items.amber: The 3200ms pulse is the surface's one semantic amber and it is defined by animation rather than hue, which is exactly why it cannot be confused with a warning. Motion is what makes it mean 'now'.
items.screenshot: Not a still — but a settled answer photographed twice a second apart is pixel-identical, while the same answer mid-flight shows one dot glowing brighter and a bar part-way grown.

items.name: Screen-reader script
items.purpose: To specify what this surface says with the same precision as what it looks like, because glyph silhouettes buy a blind manager nothing.
items.anatomy: The full announcement order for a landed answer: 'Answer.' → [headline sentence] → 'Checked 5 sources in 2.1 seconds, show the steps, button.' → 'Figures for this answer.' → each tile: '[label], [value] [unit], [direction word] [delta] [unit], [verdict word], versus [comparison]' or '[label], no data, [reason]' or '[label], [value], updated from [prior] at [time]' → 'Worst first, ranked list, 5 items' → each bar: '[name], [value] [unit], position [n] of [total]', the top row adding the word 'worst' → 'Over time, chart. Legend: this year, solid line; last year, dashed line.' → the chart's spoken summary sentence → 'Outside data, from [publisher], read [date], not TradeIQ data' → each outside figure with 'outside figure, source [n]' → 'Notice: this answer may be incomplete…' → 'Three follow-up questions' → 'Sources, 5 items' → each source row → the actions row.
items.states: LIVE — the rail announces 'Step 3 of 4, share of shelf' on change, throttled to one per 800ms, torn down on completion. THRESHOLDS — 'Still working on share of shelf', 'Writing the answer', each once. ERROR — severity first: 'Error. [message]. Try again, button.' STOPPED — 'Stopped. The answer is incomplete.' OFFLINE — 'No connection. Ask TradeIQ needs one.' SESSION ENDED — '…Your answers are still on screen.' SENT — 'Question sent' on send. PANEL SUPPRESSED — the provenance sentence, as prose, never as an error.
items.behaviour: TWO CORRECTIONS, both places where the spoken channel had been overreaching what the product knows. (1) THE LEGEND NAMES THE CHANNEL, NOT THE COLOUR: 'this year, solid line; last year, dashed line.' The previous draft said 'solid amber; dashed terracotta', which contradicted this item's own closing claim and handed a blind manager the one channel she cannot use. (2) THE FOCUS ROW NO LONGER CLAIMS INTENT. It announces 'position 1 of 11, worst' and nothing more. The lit object is derived client-side from index 0; the sentence above may actually be about the third outlet, and a sighted reader can re-read the sentence against the glow while a blind one has been TOLD which one it is. The stronger phrase — 'the one this answer is about' — is restored the day the orchestrator emits `focus: {artifactId, index}`, and not before. Every severity level carries its semanticLabel in the same token as its glyph and hue — 'Critical', 'Watch', 'On target', 'Held'. Every icon button takes a required non-empty semanticLabel as a constructor argument. Decorative elements — the caret, the initials disc, the rail's connecting line, the separation rules — are ExcludeSemantics. Numbers are announced as words: 'zero point six seconds', 'minus 19 points'.
items.modes: Identical in all three skins. Veld changes nothing here — a screen reader does not care about glare, and the two modes are orthogonal.
items.accessibility: This item is the accessibility specification.
items.amber: The live pulse degrades to the word 'Live' through the same code path it uses under reduce-motion — one path, not two, so it cannot rot.
items.screenshot: Not visual. Read aloud, a landed answer takes roughly forty seconds and never says the word 'amber', 'orange', 'red' or 'green' — only 'worst', 'bad', 'on target', 'held', 'no data', 'updated from', 'solid line' and 'dashed line'.

items.name: Too-long, too-many, none-at-all
items.purpose: The declared limits of every list and string on this surface, so an overflow is a designed state rather than a clipped one.
items.anatomy: QUESTION: soft counter at 450 chars (mono 12 ink-3), hard stop at 1000 with a 2dp bad bottom rule and a message with a filled triangle. Bubble clamps at 6 rendered lines with a 'Show the full question' row. HEADLINE: ≤160 visible characters, else it is body — the cap is on the parser, not the paint. PROSE: uncapped. TILES: 1–6 by schema; 5 or 6 make a 2×3; the grid collapses to one column below 272dp of panel inner width, which at a 360dp screen (288dp inner) keeps 2×2 on every phone the product ships to. BARS: 1–12 by schema; 6 shown, then 'Show all N'; labels take two lines before any truncation; values take the compact formatter, then a scale floor of 11px, then their own line beneath the track. SOURCES: 10 by wire cap; 4 shown, then 'Show all N'. FOLLOW-UPS: 3 by parser cap. STEPS: 8 shown (first 2, last 5, and a '… 4 more' row). ERROR MESSAGE: 160 characters, newlines collapsed, replaced by a fixed sentence when it exceeds or looks like a trace. LABELS: outlet names take two lines before middle truncation; a status word is never truncated before a name is; English strings are written to occupy no more than 60% of the available space, and every label wraps to two lines at every size.
items.states: NONE-AT-ALL for each: no tiles → the tile block is dropped; no bars → dropped; no readable chart points → one honest line in the block's slot; no sources → absent unless a search ran, in which case one line says it found nothing; no follow-ups → absent; no artifacts at all → no panel; unprovenanced artifacts → no panel plus one line; no answer text but artifacts present → no empty prose block. In every case the container is dropped, never rendered empty — an empty panel reads as a bug and a dropped one reads as an answer that did not need figures.
items.behaviour: Afrikaans runs a median 1.11× and p90 1.40× longer than English, which wrapping handles and a width axis does not — so nothing here has a fixed width, no label is fitted by condensing, and every two-line allowance is real. At 2.0× every row grows, every grid collapses on a MEASURED width threshold rather than a scale guess, and no element is pinned by height. Tap targets are 48dp on Console and Field (the Android floor; the previous draft used the 44dp iOS figure throughout, on an Android-first product) and 56dp in Veld.
items.modes: Veld halves the density: rows 64, gutter 24, block gap 40, targets 56, and the tile grid collapses to one column unconditionally. Fewer things, further apart, because precision is what you lose outdoors, not patience.
items.accessibility: Every 'Show all N' row is a labelled button naming its count and announcing its expanded state. Truncated text always has its full value available: through the expansion row, through long-press copy, or through the semantic label, which is never the truncated string. Nothing on this surface is readable only by hovering.
items.amber: None of these states introduces or removes amber; the ledger's count is independent of how many items a list holds, which is the point of budgeting objects rather than pixels.
items.screenshot: A ranked block showing six rows — two of them with names running to a second line — and a quiet 'Show all 11' row beneath; a sources group showing four rows and 'Show all 9 sources'; a question bubble clamped at six lines with 'Show the full question' under it.

openQuestions:
TYPEFACE CONFLICT — unchanged and still needs an owner's word before any golden is written. The brief fixes Onest for prose and JetBrains Mono for every figure and machine identifier; refine-cinematic.json specifies Archivo Variable as the single UI, figure and display face with Mono narrowed to identifiers, and builds a −2.03 MB footprint argument on top of it. I have followed the brief. Three consequences I decided alone. (1) Archivo's 88–112 wdth axis is load-bearing in the type scale; Onest has none, so every wdth value is dropped and the emphasis is carried by weight and tracking — the two or three labels the spec wanted to condense must now wrap or go icon-only. (2) 'Onest never renders a figure' means every digit inside a running sentence goes mono; I have made that a real, testable rule (0.94em, baseline- and height-matched, in the memoised inline-span pass) but it visibly changes the texture of every sentence and should be seen on a device before it is committed. (3) Both families now ship and Mono is used far beyond the identifier role, so the −2.03 MB saving is not real; re-measure with pyftsubset before that number appears in a commit message.

OUTSIDE DATA HAS NO SCHEMA — and this revision now ships a Phase-0 answer rather than a Phase-1 promise. Verified: tileSchema and rankedBarsSchema in backend/src/modules/assistant/figures.ts are both .strict() with label/value/unit/delta/comparedTo/meter and no provenance, so a Shoprite-website price and a TradeIQ stock count are the same object on the wire, and the separation lives only in the system prompt, which the brief forbids. The new unprovenanced-figures rule closes it structurally today: a turn that ran any web tool and carries any untagged figure renders NO figures at all — the panel is dropped, the prose stands, and one line says why. That is dull and correct and it is losing real information on every web-touched turn, so the schema (origin / readAt / publisher on the figure artifact, plus an outside flag on inline runs) should be Phase 0, not later. THE RESIDUAL RISK I could not close: prose figures are not suppressed, because suppressing an answer's sentences leaves the manager with nothing. So on a web-touched turn a scraped price can still appear unmarked inside a sentence. Someone needs to decide whether that is tolerable for one release or whether web tools should be withheld until the schema lands.

WHAT THE FOCUS OBJECT IS — unchanged, and now with a consequence. The lit object is derived client-side and deterministically (ranked bars' first item, else the trend chart's primary series, else nothing), which is honest and needs no new field, but it is an inference: the headline may be about the third bar. I have therefore DOWNGRADED the screen-reader string from 'the one this answer is about' to 'position 1 of 11, worst', because the spoken channel must not assert what the visual one merely implies. A `focus: {artifactId, index}` field on the turn would restore the stronger phrase and make the light land where the sentence points. Worth asking whether the orchestrator can emit one cheaply.

THE NAV UNDERBAR IS NOW COUNTED, AND IT COSTS A SLOT. The ledger no longer exempts chrome, so on a landed answer the screen carries two amber objects: the nav pill's active underbar and the answer's one lit thing. That is inside the brief's ceiling of two and it is now true rather than asserted. The alternative the critic offered — suppressing the nav underbar while a panel is lit — I rejected, because a wayfinding indicator that changes colour depending on what is on the page teaches the wrong thing about what the indicator means. If the owner disagrees, the change is one line in the arbiter and it takes the landed count to one.

NEW IS GONE FROM THE HEADER. The critic was right that two 48dp targets 8dp apart in the top-right, one of them destructive-adjacent, is the worst reachable point on a 6.5in phone. I did not take the proposed fix of moving it to the nav pill's action circle, because the owner has assigned that circle to 'raise a task / assign a visit' and a route-local override would give one control two meanings. Instead New is deleted: starting over lives at the foot of the history sheet, next to the sentence that names its consequence. If the owner wants a route-local primary action circle after all, this is where that decision lands.

VELD IS NOW MANUAL-ONLY ON THIS ROUTE. Solar-elevation entry is disabled here and the skin cycle sits in the header, because the previous draft could be entered automatically and had no exit control anywhere on the screen. The larger question is still open and underneath it: should Ask TradeIQ be reachable from a field agent's app at all? Today it is manager-only and gated. If it stays that way, the Veld skin of this surface serves one manager in a car park, and its per-component golden cost may not be worth paying in the first release. My recommendation is a Veld smoke test rather than a full golden set, sequenced last.

THE INCOMPLETE NOTICE IS A STRING MATCH. I lift the server's BUDGET_NOTICE constant out of the prose to render it as a component. It degrades safely, but a `notice` event or a field on `done` carrying the reason would be cleaner — the orchestrator already distinguishes rounds, time, cost and repeat internally, and I have written four texts for those four reasons that cannot currently be shown, because only one string reaches the client.

RECONCILIATION NEEDS A PRIOR VALUE AND A TIME. The new updated-figure state (gap #398) renders 'Updated from 61% at 14:22', which the client can only do if it holds the previous artifact in memory — it does, for the life of the turn — and if a patch carries a timestamp. If a patch can arrive after the transcript has been rebuilt, or if the server ever replaces an artifact without the client having seen the earlier one, the line must degrade to 'Updated at 14:22' with no prior value. I have specified that fallback but not verified which of those the orchestrator actually does.

ARTIFACT ORDER. The direction's Screen 2 specifies tiles, then bars, then chart. `arrangeAnswerArtifacts` currently ranks stat_tiles 0, everything else 1, ranked_bars 2, so the chart lands above the bars. The one-line rank change (stat_tiles 0, ranked_bars 1, others 2) changes an existing test's expectations — flagging rather than assuming.

VOICE. No speech package in pubspec.yaml and no microphone permission declared. The slot is now four lines and four invariants rather than a full recorder design. Whether it becomes an OS dictation handoff (cheap, Phase 1) or a funded in-app recorder is not mine to decide; what is not negotiable is that it never renders disabled and never auto-sends.

CONVERSATION HISTORY IS A SESSION, NOT AN ARCHIVE. ChatController holds messages in memory, caps replayed history at 20 turns, and drops everything on clear() or on leaving the screen. The sheet says exactly that and has no delete, rename or pin, because none exist. If Phase 2 introduces real conversation rows, this sheet becomes a genuinely different component and should be redesigned rather than extended.
principles: Darkness is the room; the answer is the light. One sentence, one panel, one lit object — and the light is counted, not asserted: two amber objects in Night with nothing exempt, the nav's underbar and the one thing, handed between the running step, the focus bar and the send key by a single arbiter that cannot return two. Separation is space first and a three-to-one rule second; no decorative token is ever the only cue. Severity leaves the amber band entirely. Figures are mono and tabular, animate once, never tween between two real values — and a figure that changes says so. Every container is dropped rather than rendered empty. Motion is allowed; it must always also be a word.
